scale.Confirmed: Announced by the company or shown in an official source.
scale.Likely: Multiple credible outlets or hard evidence (certifications, databases, supply chain), but no official word.
scale.Rumor: One or few sources, an estimate, or a leaker claim. Plausible but unverified.
scale.Shaky: Weak sourcing, conflicting reports, a bad track record, or a guess presented as news.
scale.Debunked: Contradicted by the company or by clear evidence.

items.title: Oppo has suspended the Find X10 Ultra
items.expected: Was expected in the first half of 2027
items.claim: Oppo has put its Find X10 Ultra camera flagship on hold, leaving the Find X10 Pro Max as its top phone of this generation.
items.why: From Digital Chat Station on Weibo, relayed by GSMArena, Android Authority and 9to5Google. DCS has a good Oppo record but gave no reason; outlets speculate that soaring memory prices are to blame, and Xiaomi's 18 Ultra has also been reported cancelled. Oppo has not commented, and 'suspended' could mean delayed rather than dead, so it stays a Rumor.

items.title: Apple merges the Action button into Camera Control on 2027 iPhones
items.expected: iPhones from the second half of 2027 (leak)
items.claim: Starting with iPhones released in the second half of 2027, the separate Action button goes away; a press of Camera Control opens the camera and a long press runs the assigned Action.
items.why: From Weibo leaker Instant Digital, relayed by MacRumors, 9to5Mac and GSMArena. The leaker has a mixed record: an earlier claim of a simplified Camera Control for iPhone 18 did not happen. The iPhone Duo already ships without an Action button, which makes the idea plausible, but there is no second source.

items.title: Windows 11 27H2 is a 'full OS swap', not Windows 12
items.expected: Second half of 2027; Insider testing earlier than June
items.claim: Microsoft's 2027 Windows update, 27H2, is a major platform-level release focused on quality, with a new default wallpaper, Insider testing starting well before June, and the Windows 11 name kept.
items.why: Reported by The Verge from unnamed sources and relayed by TechRadar. One report, though The Verge's Windows sourcing is usually solid. Naming is reportedly not fully final, and Microsoft has not announced 27H2.

items.title: Android 17 QPR2 reaches Pixels in November instead of December
items.claim: Google skipped the usual first-Tuesday November Pixel patch because it is shipping Android 17 QPR2 early, in November.
items.why: A Reddit theory relayed by Android Authority, based on security-bulletin tags ('17-qpr2-next:2026-11-01'), a large batch of Pixel driver changes and November-dated release-candidate builds on BetaWiki. That is circumstantial: Google has not confirmed anything, and Android 16 QPR2 shipped in December last year. Update Nov 10: Google released Android 17 QPR2 to Pixels with the November Pixel Drop and security patch, a month earlier than Android 16 QPR2 last year.
items.outcome: Correct. Android 17 QPR2 reached Pixel phones on Nov 10 alongside the November Pixel Drop, as the bulletin-tag theory predicted, instead of in December.

items.title: Oppo's Find N7 foldable launches in Europe
items.expected: Not announced (Oppo foldables usually launch early in the year)
items.claim: Oppo's next book-style foldable, the Find N7, will be sold in Europe, a first for an Oppo-branded foldable.
items.why: Oppo reportedly confirmed European availability to creator Nixanbal (via GSMArena and 9to5Google). It comes from the company, but second-hand and without a date or price; a March 2027 timing is only an inference from past launches. The rumored wide form factor is not part of this claim.

items.title: The vanilla Xiaomi 18 launches in December with 100W charging
items.claim: A standard Xiaomi 18 is still coming this year, around December in China, with 100W wired charging, the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6, a 200MP main camera and a 7,200mAh battery.
items.why: A new 3C certification (via GSMArena) lists a Xiaomi phone with 100W charging that is believed, not confirmed, to be the Xiaomi 18. The December timing and other specs come from earlier leaks. Certification is hard evidence that a device exists, but its identity is inferred and Xiaomi has not mentioned the base model. Update Nov 12: a dealer poster on Weibo shows offline retailers in China taking refundable blind deposits for the standard Xiaomi 18 (GSMArena, Gizmochina), and Digital Chat Station tips a 2nm mid-size model with up to 16GB/1TB. Dealer pre-orders plus the 3C listing are hard signs of a near launch, so this moves to Likely; Xiaomi itself has not confirmed a date or specs. Update Nov 17: XiaomiTime reports a Xiaomi Weibo poster announcing blind bookings for the 'Xiaomi 18 Standard Edition', and Lei Jun was photographed with a white phone believed to be the Xiaomi 18 at the APEC CEO Summit (Gizmochina). The phone is now effectively official, but Xiaomi has not given a date or confirmed the 100W and battery specs, so it stays Likely. Update Nov 18: tipster Debayan Roy (Gadgetsdata) posted a purported live image of a white Xiaomi 18 with a metal frame, a three-camera square island and no rear screen, and lists 100W wired charging, the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 and a 200MP main camera, but a battery of about 7,000mAh (not 7,200mAh) and a 50MP telephoto instead of the 200MP periscope from earlier leaks (GSMArena, Gadgets360). The 100W and chip details agree; the exact battery size is now disputed. Stays Likely. Update Nov 20: Xiaomi's own online store in China now takes blind pre-reservations for the Xiaomi 18, still without a date, design or specs (GSMArena). That makes a near launch even more certain, but the 100W and battery details remain leaks, so it stays Likely.

items.title: vivo is developing a wide-screen phone for a 2027 launch
items.claim: vivo is working on a wide-screen phone aimed at a 2027 launch, following similar reports about other Android brands.
items.why: GSMArena reported the claim on Nov 6. It is a single-outlet tip without specs, codenames or an official vivo comment, so it stays a Rumor.

items.title: Lucid teases a cheaper Cosmos EV aimed under $50,000
items.claim: Lucid is preparing a cheaper Cosmos model positioned under $50,000, shown in a new teaser video and images.
items.why: Electrek covered Lucid's Nov 6 teaser explicitly framing a sub-$50,000 Cosmos. That is company marketing rather than a full unveil, so the name and price target look Likely, while timing, range and powertrain details remain unannounced.

items.title: Honor is developing a Robot Phone 2 for a 2027 launch
items.claim: Honor is working on a second-generation Robot Phone that could launch in 2027.
items.why: Android Authority reported a leak on Nov 6 that a Robot Phone 2 is in the works for next year. Honor has not confirmed a sequel, and the original Robot Phone details and sales traction are still thin in English coverage, so this stays a single-source Rumor.

items.title: Tesla winds down Cybertruck production around mid-2027 to free Giga Texas for Cybercab
items.claim: Tesla will wind down Cybertruck production at Gigafactory Texas around the middle of 2027 to make room for more Cybercab production.
items.why: Elon Musk stated this directly on X on Nov 6, 2026, and major outlets including Electrek, TechCrunch and The Verge reported it the same day. Inventory runoff, parts support and any price changes after the wind-down were not detailed in the post.
items.outcome: Confirmed as stated by Musk on Nov 6, 2026. Production wind-down targeted for around mid-2027 at Giga Texas; Cybercab cited as the reason.

items.title: Tesla's SI6 inference chip targets ~80x HW4 compute around 2029-2030, with a chiplet Dojo D3 for training
items.claim: Tesla's refreshed accelerator roadmap renames AI chips to SI (Super Intelligence); SI6 aims for about 80x HW4/SI4 compute and 9x memory around 2029-2030, while Dojo D3 becomes a chiplet design with stacked HBM aimed at scalable and space-ready training.
items.why: Tom's Hardware reported the roadmap from a Tesla presentation dated around Nov 4-6, 2026, including a table that maps SI4 (current car inference), SI5/SI6 and Dojo D3. The SI branding matches Musk's recent 'Super Intelligence' language, and HW4/AI4 already shipped, so the rename of current silicon is straightforward. Absolute TOPS numbers are estimates derived from Musk's old HW3/HW4 multipliers, and D3's schedule, process and performance are still blank on the slide, so this is Likely rather than Confirmed company product timing.

items.title: Apple launches OLED touchscreen MacBook Pros and an M6 lineup at its Oct 28 launch
items.claim: At its Oct 28 launch Apple will announce OLED touchscreen 14- and 16-inch MacBook Pros (M5 Pro/Max), an OLED iPad mini, a 14-inch M6 MacBook Pro and an M6 iMac, with sales from Nov 6.
items.why: The date is now official: on Oct 19 Apple's Greg Joswiak posted the invite for a 'Pro and tell' media experience in Los Angeles on Oct 28 at 10 a.m. PT, one day after Bloomberg's 'on or around Oct 27'. The tagline points to the MacBook Pro, but Apple has not named any product, so the line-up remains a Bloomberg report. Supporting evidence: Bloomberg called the Oct 13 launch correctly; an unreleased iPad mini Smart Folio (A3632) appeared on Apple's French regulatory site; and Gurman says Apple Stores plan an overnight reset on Nov 5-6. The chip question has largely settled: Gurman, 9to5Mac and MacRumors now all say the OLED models use the existing M5 Pro/Max, with M6 only in the entry 14-inch MacBook Pro and iMac. Update Oct 26: part of the claim is already confirmed. Apple announced the OLED iPad mini (8.5-inch, A20 Pro) by press release, with pre-orders Oct 28 and availability Nov 6, matching the reported Nov 6 sales date. Greg Joswiak then teased an 'exciting week', and Gurman's Oct 25 newsletter repeats that the touchscreen MacBook Pros come Wednesday. The MacBook Pro and iMac parts are still unannounced. We will resolve this on Oct 28. Update Oct 27: more of the claim is now confirmed, a day early. Apple announced the 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 ($1,999) and the iMac with M6 ($1,499) by press release, both with pre-orders Oct 28 and availability Nov 6, matching Gurman's line-up and the Nov 6 sales date. Only the OLED touchscreen 14- and 16-inch MacBook Pros remain unannounced; Gurman still expects them Wednesday. We keep this at Likely and will resolve it on Oct 28. Update Oct 28 (before the 10 a.m. PT event): Apple CEO John Ternus posted a teaser video on X this morning, and a leaker found Dynamic Island assets in macOS 27. Bloomberg adds that Apple has discussed $2,899 for the 14-inch OLED model ($400 more than the current M5 Pro model). Apple has still not confirmed the OLED models, so this stays Likely until the announcement. Update Oct 29: Apple announced the 14- and 16-inch MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display (tandem OLED, touch, Dynamic Island) on Oct 28 with M5 Pro and M5 Max, from $2,899 and $3,399, with pre-orders that day and availability Nov 6.

sources.name: Apple Newsroom (MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display)
Apple Newsroom (14-inch MacBook Pro with M6)

items.outcome: True. Every part of the claim happened: Apple announced OLED touchscreen 14- and 16-inch MacBook Pros with M5 Pro/Max on Oct 28 (Bloomberg's $2,899 price was also right), and the OLED iPad mini, M6 14-inch MacBook Pro and M6 iMac all went on sale Nov 6 as promised. One detail differed in timing: those three were announced by press release on Oct 26-27, ahead of the event. Apple calls the new display 'PROLED XDR', and the mini-LED models stay on sale. MacRumors confirmed US and global availability starting Nov 6, with Australia/NZ first.

items.title: Standard iPhone 18 and iPhone 18e arrive in spring 2027
items.claim: Apple is splitting its iPhone releases: Pro and foldable models in fall, the standard iPhone 18 and 18e in spring.
items.why: Reported repeatedly by Mark Gurman and echoed by several outlets. The fall 2026 lineup (iPhone 18 Pro and the foldable iPhone Duo) matched the split. Apple has not confirmed the spring models or date. Update Nov 18: Korea's ETNews says Samsung Display and LG Display will start mass-producing OLED panels for the iPhone 18 and iPhone Air 2 in late December and early January, lining up with a March 2027 launch (MacRumors). Supply-chain timing that fits the spring window; Apple still has not confirmed anything, so it stays Likely.

items.title: Galaxy S27 family has four models, including a compact S27 Pro
items.claim: Samsung will release the Galaxy S27, S27+, S27 Pro and S27 Ultra.
items.why: Model numbers for all four (SM-S952U, SM-S956U, SM-S958U and a global dual-SIM SM-S957B/DS) appeared in the GSMA IMEI database, which is strong evidence a phone exists but does not confirm names, specs or launch dates. On Oct 16, two more model numbers (SM-S9570 and SM-S9580, believed to be the Pro and Ultra) appeared in China's MIIT certification database. On Oct 20 leaked third-party screen protectors showed only the S27, S27+ and S27 Ultra (6.27, 6.66 and 6.89 inches), without the Pro. Accessory leaks are less reliable than certification databases, so we keep this at Likely for now. On Oct 22-23, batteries for the S27 Pro (EB-BS957CBY) and S27 Ultra (EB-BS958DBY) passed Safety Korea certification, another regulatory sign that a Pro model exists. Update Nov 4: import-export records on the NBD trade platform list European versions of all four (SM-S952B, S956B, S957B and S958B), with chips and screen sizes (6.3, 6.7, 6.5 and 6.9 inches). More evidence for a four-model lineup, still not official.

items.title: Galaxy S27 Unpacked lands around Feb 24, 2027
items.claim: Samsung will hold its Galaxy S27 Unpacked in late February 2027, possibly on Feb 24.
items.why: This is an estimate extrapolated from past schedules (Jan 17, 2024; Jan 22, 2025; Feb 25, 2026) and early One UI 9.5 firmware testing, not a leak from Samsung. Samsung usually sends invitations about two weeks before the show. Re-rated Shaky on Oct 19: Korean tipster Lanzuk, who has a solid Samsung record, now says Samsung is aiming for early January 2027, which contradicts the late-February guess.

items.title: Galaxy S27 parts ramp to mass production in mid-October
items.claim: Some Galaxy S27 components entered mass production in September, with all four models ramping in mid-October.
items.why: Single-source report from ZDNet Korea relayed by SammyGuru and iDevice. Samsung has not commented.

items.title: NVIDIA RTX 50 Super cards debut at CES 2027
items.claim: NVIDIA will launch the RTX 5060 Super (12GB), 5070 Super (18GB) and 5070 Ti/5080 Super (24GB) around CES 2027.
items.why: Earlier reports named CES 2027, but a later September 2026 report says NVIDIA has no RTX 50 Super plans for 2027 and the refresh may not ship. The dates have moved repeatedly and the sources conflict. On Oct 12 Taiwan's BenchLife reported a 24GB RTX 5080 for Q1 2027 that would replace the 16GB card; it is unclear whether that is the rumored 5080 Super or a different plan (tracked separately below).

items.title: NVIDIA RTX 60 series slips to 2028
items.claim: The next GeForce generation will miss 2027 and reach retail in 2028; AMD will have only one RDNA 5 GPU in 2027.
items.why: Based on a leaker's claims reported by Club386 and a Verge report that the lineup could miss 2027. Neither company has confirmed. On Oct 12 the same leaker, Kepler_L2, said AMD is unlikely to even announce RDNA 5 before Computex (June) 2027 and that a later 2027 reveal is more likely. AMD has published no schedule.

items.title: Intel Nova Lake-S desktop CPUs debut at CES 2027
items.claim: Intel will launch Core Ultra 400 'Nova Lake-S' desktop chips at CES 2027, with first retail models in Q1 2027.
items.why: Several outlets reported a CES 2027 debut and Q4 2026 mass production, based on leakers and supply-chain reports. Update Oct 30: on Intel's Oct 29 earnings call, CEO Lip-Bu Tan said Nova Lake is 'tracking ahead of schedule' and Intel will 'share more at CES in January', which supports the CES timing. He did not promise a CES launch or Q1 retail availability, so we keep this at Likely until Intel gives dates.

items.title: AMD Zen 6 desktop chips show up at CES 2027
items.claim: AMD's Zen 6 'Olympic Ridge' desktop CPUs will be revealed at CES 2027 with retail from March to June 2027.
items.why: Trade-press reports of a delay from earlier plans; retail window is an estimate. AMD has not confirmed. Update Nov 20: a Chiphell leaker now claims a slip to the second half of 2027 (see the separate rumor), which conflicts with the March-June retail window. AMD still teases CES news, so this stays a Rumor.

items.title: OpenAI's first device is a screenless smart speaker with a camera
items.claim: The first Jony Ive-designed OpenAI device is a hockey-puck-sized speaker with a camera and sensors, priced around $200-$300.
items.why: Form factor and price come from reports and leaks that OpenAI has not confirmed. One piece is firm: a court filing says no shipping before the end of February 2027.

items.title: Apple unveils smart glasses at WWDC 2027
items.claim: Apple will show privacy-focused smart glasses at WWDC 2027 and ship them in late 2027.
items.why: Reporting traces back mainly to Bloomberg's Mark Gurman, who also warns it could slip to late 2028 or 2029. The camera design decision was reported as not final. Update Nov 11: Chinese inspection-equipment maker Quick Intelligent Equipment told investors it is involved in 'Apple's AI glasses and new smart earphones projects' (Securities Times via MacRumors). That supports the glasses being in development but says nothing about a WWDC reveal or ship date. Update Nov 15: in Power On, Gurman repeated the plan to unveil the glasses (codename N50) at WWDC in June 2027 and ship before year-end, with no AR display and Siri controlling actions in paired iPhone apps; he warns that late software and AI work could delay it. More detail from the same reporter, so it stays a Rumor.

items.title: PS6 and the next Xbox slip because of the memory shortage
items.claim: Sony's PS6 and Microsoft's next Xbox (Project Helix) will launch later than planned because of high memory prices.
items.why: Sony's CEO said the PS6 launch date is still undecided because of the component shortage, and Microsoft's new CEO admitted the next Xbox is affected. The 2028-2029 timeframe for PS6 is a report, not a statement. On Oct 20 Fortune reported, citing people familiar with Microsoft's plans, that the Project Helix console is planned for 2028, with a next-gen Xbox handheld possibly by the end of 2027; see our separate price rumor. Update Nov 3 (reconciling with our PS6 reveal rumor): a separate insider claim puts a PS6 announcement in early March 2027. That does not contradict this rumor: an announcement says little about the launch date, and Sony still says the PS6 launch timing is undecided. We keep this Likely because both companies have tied their plans to the memory shortage, but the 2028-2029 PS6 window remains a report, not a fact.

items.title: Tesla unveils Optimus V3 before the end of 2026
items.claim: Tesla will publicly show its Optimus V3 humanoid robot in 2026.
items.why: Elon Musk had targeted a July-August window that passed without a reveal. On the Oct 21 Q3 earnings call Tesla said early production of Optimus had begun on its Fremont line, but it did not present a new version, and Musk promised only a video 'within a month or two' showing unscripted tasks, with deliveries to outside companies around the end of 2027. Treat Tesla timelines with caution.

items.title: Microsoft's next Xbox console costs $1,200-1,800 and launches in 2028
items.claim: Microsoft's Project Helix console will cost between $1,200 and $1,800 unless Microsoft subsidizes it, and will launch in 2028, with a next-generation Xbox handheld by the end of 2027.
items.why: One report, from Fortune, based on unnamed sources; GameSpot, Engadget and Ars Technica relayed it. The price is a projected range that depends on whether Microsoft eats some of the cost, and memory shortages make high prices plausible. Xbox CTO Scott Van Vliet disputed the same story's account of the handheld's software, though not the price or timing. Microsoft has announced no date or price.

items.title: OnePlus readies a Turbo 7 Pro with an unreleased Snapdragon 'Pro' chip and 100W charging
items.claim: OnePlus is developing a Turbo Pro (possibly Turbo 7 Pro) with a new 3nm Snapdragon 8 Gen 5 Pro (SM8845 Pro), a 6.78-inch 1.5K 185Hz screen, a 200MP main camera and a 9,000mAh battery, launching around the end of the year.
items.why: From Digital Chat Station, a prolific Weibo tipster with a decent record, in a post he later edited; Android Authority reported it. Qualcomm has not announced a Snapdragon 8 Gen 5 Pro, and OnePlus has not mentioned the phone. The timing is vague. GSMArena adds that the tipster also mentioned a clip-on external fan accessory, and that the screen, camera and battery match the OnePlus 16; the same SM8845 Pro chip is rumored for the iQOO Z12 Turbo/iQOO 16R. Update Nov 2: another Weibo tipster says a OnePlus Turbo 7 will use the unannounced 'Snapdragon 8 Gen 6' with a 200MP main camera and a 185Hz screen, and launch by the end of the year; GSMArena notes it may be the same phone. Similar details from a second tipster, but Qualcomm and OnePlus have announced nothing, so it stays a Rumor. Update Nov 18: a OnePlus phone with model number PYP110, which Digital Chat Station says is the Turbo 7 Pro, passed China's 3C certification with 100W chargers. DCS adds a 185Hz screen (165Hz system-wide), a 200MP main camera, a battery of at least 9,000mAh, no built-in fan and a December launch; a tipster on X lists the SM8845 Pro chip and about 10,000mAh. The certification is hard evidence that the phone exists and charges at 100W, so this moves to Likely; the chip name, battery size and date are still unconfirmed.

items.title: NVIDIA's RTX 6060 doesn't arrive until 2029
items.claim: NVIDIA's budget RTX 6060 will launch around 2029, well after the higher-end RTX 60 cards, and may not match the PS6's gaming performance.
items.why: Leaker Kepler posted this in a NeoGAF thread, and TechRadar relayed it via Wccftech. He framed it as a guess based on NVIDIA's past habit of delaying low-end cards during shortages, not as inside information. It assumes the RTX 60 series itself lands in 2028, which is also only a rumor (see our RTX 60 entry).

items.title: Honor Win 2 and Win 2 RT launch in October
items.claim: Honor's Win 2 and Win 2 RT phones launch this month with 100W/90W charging and 10,000mAh+ batteries.
items.why: Honor announced on Oct 12 that the Win 2 series would launch Oct 21, and it did: the Win 2 arrived in China with a 10,100mAh battery and 100W wired charging, so the battery and 100W parts of the claim held up. Honor launched the Win RT 2 and Win Turbo 2 alongside it, but we could not verify the 90W charging figure the original leak gave for the other models.
items.outcome: Confirmed: the Win 2 launched in China on Oct 21 with a 10,100mAh battery and 100W charging. The 90W claim for other models is unverified.

items.title: OPPO Find X10 launches worldwide on Oct 21
items.claim: OPPO's Find X10 goes on sale on Oct 21.
items.why: We first rated this Shaky because the only clue was a UK promotion ending Oct 21. OPPO then confirmed an Oct 21 global launch, and on the day it published prices and opened orders in Europe (Finland: EUR 1,499 and EUR 1,799). But 'on sale' only partly held: European deliveries start Nov 2, Singapore pre-orders open Oct 22 with deliveries from Oct 26, and India launches Oct 22.
items.outcome: Mostly confirmed: launched and orderable on Oct 21, but phones ship from Nov 2 in Europe, so it was not in buyers' hands that day.

items.title: Claude 6 arrives around May 2027 and GPT-7 around Jul-Aug 2027
items.claim: Anthropic's next flagship lands around May 2027 and OpenAI's around July-August 2027.
items.why: These are prediction-market and blog forecasts. Neither company has announced model names or dates.

items.title: Galaxy S27 Ultra may switch to Exynos 2700 because Snapdragon overheats
items.claim: Samsung found the Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 overheating in S27 Ultra testing and may use its own Exynos 2700 chip if Qualcomm doesn't fix it by mid-October.
items.why: The report came from Korean outlet SEDaily and was relayed by SamMobile and others. Qualcomm told 9to5Google on Oct 17 the overheating reports are 'inaccurate', and its CMO Don McGuire says there are 'no systemic thermal issues'. A separate Oct 16 MoneyToday report says Samsung has dropped the Exynos plan for the Ultra because of Exynos supply limits and memory costs, and the Ultra will use Snapdragon only. Samsung has not commented. Single-sourced, denied, and now contradicted by another report. An Oct 19 Lanzuk leak (via SamMobile) also says the Ultra may use Qualcomm's chip exclusively. Update Oct 30: Ice Universe says there is still no sign of an Exynos 2700 S27 Ultra for Europe, while Korea remains undecided, so the Snapdragon-only reading still has more support. Update Nov 4: NBD trade records list the European S27 Ultra (SM-S958B/DS) with Qualcomm's SM8975 (Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6), while only the S27 and S27+ get the Exynos 2700. Europe is the market where an Exynos Ultra would most likely appear, so this weighs further against the claim. Not yet Debunked, because trade listings are not final and Samsung has said nothing. Update Nov 6: tipster yeux1122 (via GSMArena) says Samsung will use Snapdragon for both the S27 Pro and S27 Ultra even in South Korea, for cost reasons, despite Exynos 2700 test results. With Korea the last market in question, the Exynos Ultra claim has almost nothing left supporting it; it stays Shaky only until Samsung announces the phones.

items.title: Galaxy S27+ drops ultra-wideband (UWB)
items.claim: The Galaxy S27+ may lose UWB, a feature Samsung has offered for years.
items.why: Leaker Abhishek Yadav found two S27 models (SM-S9570 and SM-S9580, believed to be the Pro and Ultra) in China's MIIT certification database with UWB listed, and says the S27 and S27+ lack it; SammyFans reported precise tracking may be Pro/Ultra-only. The certification is real evidence for the two higher models, but the S27+ losing UWB is an inference from what is missing. Samsung has not commented.

items.title: Apple Intelligence fully launches in China with iOS 27.3 in December
items.expected: December 2026 (Apple; developer beta live since Nov 3)
items.claim: After an October beta, Apple will roll out Apple Intelligence in China with iOS 27.3 in December, without the new Siri, Image Playground or the newer Genmoji.
items.why: Reported by Bloomberg. The groundwork is confirmed: Tim Cook said on Oct 15 that a beta arrives this month after regulators approved the first features and Alibaba's Qwen models, and the SCMP reports China's MIIT granted network permits for the models. Apple has not given a date or feature list for the full launch. Update Oct 31: Apple confirmed it. Its China Newsroom says the features enter developer beta on Nov 4 and launch with iOS 27.3 in December; Siri AI and Image Playground are excluded, as Bloomberg reported, though Genmoji is in the first wave. The October beta Cook promised did not happen. Stays active until iOS 27.3 actually ships. Update Nov 4: the developer beta arrived on schedule. iOS 27.3 beta 1 (Nov 3 US, Nov 4 China) lets developers in China turn on Apple Intelligence, with Siri AI still excluded. The remaining question is the December public release.

items.title: One UI 10 is Samsung's biggest software overhaul yet
items.claim: Samsung's One UI 10 will be its biggest software overhaul yet, built around cross-app 'contextual flow', fewer menus and tighter device handoffs, possibly with paid tiers for heavy AI features.
items.why: Comes from an unnamed insider via Nokia Power User, relayed by GSMArena; tipster Ice Universe, who has a solid Samsung track record, says his own source confirms 'significant changes, unprecedented in nature'. Timing is disputed: SamMobile expects mid-2027 with the Galaxy Z Fold 9 and Flip 9, while GSMArena's reading of the insider points to the Galaxy S29. Samsung has said nothing, and the details are vague.

items.title: GTA VI comes to PC in Q1 2027
items.claim: Rockstar plans to release the PC version of Grand Theft Auto VI in the first quarter of 2027, a few months after the Nov 19 console launch.
items.why: GamesBeat reports this from four anonymous industry sources; The Verge, Polygon and others relayed it, but nobody has independent confirmation. Rockstar did not comment, and its store page still lists only PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. It would be a much shorter gap than GTA V's 19-month wait for PC. Update Nov 19: the console version launched on Nov 19 and Rockstar has still not announced a PC version or date, so the Q1 2027 report remains unconfirmed.

items.title: NVIDIA swaps the RTX 5080 to 24GB in Q1 2027
items.claim: NVIDIA will release an RTX 5080 with 24GB of GDDR7 in early 2027, gradually replacing the 16GB model.
items.why: Single-source report from Taiwan's BenchLife, relayed by VideoCardz and TechPowerUp. Board partners reportedly have only verbal guidance and no design documents yet, so timing is soft. Technically easy: 3GB memory chips on the same 256-bit bus. NVIDIA has not commented. Comes amid tight RTX 5090 supply, which NVIDIA says is constrained but not discontinued. Update Oct 30: Tom's Hardware found the RTX 5080 removed from Nvidia's US store after the RTX 5090, with street prices about 2.2x the $999 MSRP. That fits a product transition but is not proof of a 24GB model; Nvidia has not commented. Update Nov 3: BenchLife, the original source, now says the 'probability is extremely high' the 24GB card misses January, because board partners expected design details in October and still have none (relayed by VideoCardz and TechRadar). Q1 is still possible but the timing is softer, so it stays Rumor. Update Nov 11: Board Channels sources (via VideoCardz, Gazlog and leaker Harukaze) say NVIDIA told board partners the planned January 2027 China launch of the 24GB card is canceled because 3GB GDDR7 chips cost about three times as much as 2GB ones, and that the 16GB RTX 5080 stays in production. NVIDIA has neither confirmed nor denied either plan. With leaks now contradicting each other, this drops to Shaky; we will mark it Debunked if NVIDIA or partners confirm the cancellation. Update Nov 12: more outlets (HotHardware, Club386, OC3D, Notebookcheck) repeated the cancellation report, but all trace back to the same Board Channels leak, and NVIDIA still has not commented, so it stays Shaky rather than Debunked.

items.title: Galaxy S27 Ultra gets thinner bezels and a thicker camera bump
items.claim: The Galaxy S27 Ultra will have 1.28mm screen bezels (vs 1.32mm on the S26 Ultra) and a 4.69mm camera bump, slightly thicker than today's.
items.why: Measurements come from leaker Ice Universe, who has a good Samsung record, relayed by SamMobile. They fit separate case leaks showing a wide camera bar on the Pro and Ultra. Small, unverified numbers; Samsung has said nothing. Update Nov 3: Android Headlines built a dummy from leaked CAD renders showing a camera bar moved higher (leaving room for magnetic accessories), the S Pen slot kept and dimensions of 163.76 x 78.25 x 7.97 mm, slightly larger than the S26 Ultra. A dummy only reflects the renders it is built from. Update Nov 10: Sonny Dickson shared dummy units of the S27 Ultra, S27 Pro and S27+, with the wide camera bar on the Ultra and Pro and an S26+-style pill module on the S27+. Like the renders, dummies show design, not the bezel or bump measurements.

items.title: OnePlus Ace 7 and Ace 7 Pro both get 200MP main cameras
items.claim: Both OnePlus Ace 7 models will use a 200MP main camera, and the Pro adds a 50MP 3.5x periscope.
items.why: From Weibo tipster Digital Chat Station, relayed by GSMArena. OnePlus has now set the launch for Oct 29 and confirmed the chips (Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 'V series' for the Ace 7, standard 8 Elite Gen 5 for the Pro) and the cooling fan, and on Oct 26 it confirmed the Pro half of the claim: a 200MP main camera plus a 3.5x periscope telephoto on the Ace 7 Pro (it did not state the periscope's resolution). The standard Ace 7's camera is still unconfirmed. We will resolve this at launch. Update Oct 29: OnePlus launched both phones with a 200MP main camera; the Pro adds a 50MP 3.5x periscope.
items.outcome: True. Both the Ace 7 and Ace 7 Pro launched on Oct 29 with 200MP main cameras, and the Pro has a 50MP 3.5x periscope telephoto, exactly as Digital Chat Station said.

items.title: Galaxy S27 series launches in early January 2027
items.claim: Samsung plans to launch the Galaxy S27, S27+, S27 Pro and S27 Ultra in early January 2027, a few weeks earlier than the S25 and S26.
items.why: From Korean tipster Lanzuk on Naver, who has a solid track record on Samsung, relayed by SamMobile and GSMArena. The leak says major hardware is finalized but Samsung is still deciding whether the Pro and Ultra get LPDDR6 and UFS 5.0 because of memory prices. GSMArena reads it more loosely as a return to the usual January-February window. Samsung has not announced anything.

items.title: PlayStation 6 costs $1,000 or more
items.claim: Memory and storage alone will cost Sony about $680 per PS6, pushing the console's price to $1,000 or more.
items.why: Leaker KeplerL2, who has a decent hardware track record, made the $680 claim on NeoGAF and earlier estimated a $960 bill of materials (in July). The $1,000 price is an inference from those cost estimates plus Sony saying it does not intend to sell hardware at significant losses, not a leaked price. Sony has not said when the PS6 launches or what it costs.

items.title: vivo X500 Ultra uses the Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6, a huge battery and a bigger 200MP telephoto
items.claim: The vivo X500 Ultra launches in China around March-April 2027 with the Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6, a flat 6.85-inch BOE LTPO screen, an ultrasonic fingerprint sensor, a 7,000-8,000mAh battery, a 50MP Sony LYT910 35mm main camera and a 200MP 1/1.2-inch telephoto.
items.why: All from Weibo tipster Digital Chat Station via GSMArena. On Oct 21 he said the latest engineering sample tests a 200MP 1/1.2-inch telephoto sensor, larger than the X300 Ultra's 1/1.4-inch. GSMArena's two write-ups disagree on the battery (about 7,000mAh on Oct 19, about 8,000mAh on Oct 21), and engineering samples often change. The chip choice is the expected default for a 2027 Ultra; vivo has not announced the phone. On Oct 23 he added that the engineering sample's 35mm main camera uses a 50MP Sony LYT910 sensor (down from 200MP on the X300 Ultra, though with larger pixels). Separately, a global model (V2660) and a Brazil 'Jovi' model appeared in an IMEI database, which supports a launch outside China but says nothing about specs. Update Nov 5: leaker Yogesh Brar (via Android Authority) says the X500 Ultra pairs a 200MP main camera with a 50MP ultrawide and a 200MP periscope, which contradicts Digital Chat Station's Oct 23 claim of a 50MP LYT910 main sensor. Two tipsters now disagree on the main camera, so we lower this to Shaky. Brar also warns the memory shortage could limit a global launch. Update Nov 8: after reports that Oppo paused the Find X10 Ultra and Xiaomi cancelled the 18 Ultra, Digital Chat Station (via GSMArena) says the X500 Ultra is still aimed at March or April 2027 in China and will use the Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6, matching the timing vivo's VP gave in September. That supports the phone still being on track, but it does not settle the conflicting camera-spec leaks, so the rating stays Shaky. Update Nov 10: Digital Chat Station now says the X500 Ultra uses two Sony LYTIA L910 sensors, for the main and ultrawide cameras, with an 'HPU' sensor in the periscope offering LOFIC and DeepPix, and repeats the Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 and March-April timing. It adds detail to his own earlier claim rather than settling the disagreement with other tipsters, so it stays Shaky.

items.title: Apple plans a bigger HomeView with a 9-inch screen on a robotic arm
items.claim: Apple is developing a higher-end HomeView smart home hub with a 9-inch screen that swivels 360 degrees on a robotic arm, for 2027 or 2028.
items.why: Reported by Bloomberg's Mark Gurman, who has a strong Apple record, in his Oct 18 newsletter. Names like 'HomeView Max' are his guesses. The timeline is far out and Apple's plans could change; the current 7-inch HomeView ships Nov 13.

items.title: Galaxy S27 and S27+ start with just 8GB of RAM
items.claim: Because of soaring memory prices, Samsung will sell 8GB/256GB versions of the Galaxy S27 and S27+ alongside 12GB/512GB models, while the S27 Pro and Ultra start at 12GB.
items.why: From leaker @kro_roe on X, relayed by SamMobile and 9to5Google. It contradicts a September leak that had the S27 keeping the S26's 12GB base, but it fits the memory shortage: Yonhap reports most of Samsung's 2027 DRAM output is already sold to big tech customers. The same leaker says Samsung may mix UFS storage generations and cut pre-order storage upgrades. Samsung has said nothing. Update Nov 4 (downgraded to Shaky): NBD trade records list all four European S27 models, including the S27 and S27+, with 12GB of RAM and 256GB of storage. That does not rule out extra 8GB versions elsewhere, but the only hard data so far points to a 12GB base, against this single-leaker claim.

items.title: Samsung launches six foldables in 2027, including a rollable Galaxy Z Slide
items.claim: Samsung's 2027 line-up will have six Galaxy Z devices: Z Flip9, Z Fold9, Z Fold9 Pro, Z Fold9 Ultra, Z TriFold2 and a rollable Z Slide, with the TriFold 2 arriving first.
items.why: From tipster @TheGalox_ on X, relayed by 9to5Google and Android Authority. Four of the names match an earlier report; the Fold9 Pro and Z Slide are new and uncorroborated. Samsung Display has shown slidable screens, but earlier reports pointed to a rollable phone in the first half of 2028, so the Slide's 2027 timing is the weakest part.

items.title: AMD's 'Gainsborough' APU powers the Steam Deck 2
items.claim: An AMD engineering sample codenamed Gainsborough, with six Zen 6-family cores and 24GB of LPDDR5-9600 in testing, is the chip for Valve's Steam Deck 2.
items.why: The benchmark listing on OpenBenchmarking is real, and kernel data places it in AMD's Zen 6 range. The Steam Deck link rests only on the codename: Gainsborough is Aerith's surname in Final Fantasy VII, and Valve's earlier Deck chips were named Aerith and Sephiroth. Its early GPU score is only slightly above the current Deck, Valve has not announced a Steam Deck 2, and TechPowerUp notes the chip could end up in other handhelds.

items.title: Huawei Mate X8 foldable launches in November
items.claim: Huawei will launch the Mate X8 in China in November with Kirin 9050/9050 Pro chips, an 8.15-inch inner and 6.5-inch cover screen, a 50MP 1/1.28-inch variable-aperture main camera, a 50MP periscope and a battery above 6,000mAh, plus a privacy-display version.
items.why: From Weibo tipster Bai Ze Guan Shan, relayed by Gizmochina and GSMArena. The timing fits Huawei's pattern (the Mate X7 launched in November 2025), but the tipster says the launch was planned alongside a new sub-brand whose timing is uncertain. Huawei has not announced anything. Update Oct 30: tipster Smart Pikachu (via Gizmochina) also lists the Mate X8 among Huawei's November products, with a Kirin 9050 Pro and a 50MP RYYB periscope. A second tipster agreeing lifts the timing a little, but Huawei has set no date; the Mate X7 launched Nov 26 last year. Update Nov 2: a Weibo tipster relayed by Huawei Central says Huawei's Star Shine sub-brand phones come in early November and the Mate X8 later in the month. Still no official date. Update Nov 11: Weibo tipster RuryRen says the Mate X8 launches in mid-to-late November, probably after the 20th, with the Kirin 9050 Pro, 16GB of RAM, storage up to 2TB and HarmonyOS 7. Huawei has now dated other November events (MateBook Fold S pre-sale Nov 14, OSTA Nov 20) but still not the Mate X8. Update Nov 13: a Chinese rumor relayed by GSMArena and Huawei Central puts the launch on Nov 24, with support for Huawei's Ruiying Z10 10x camera add-on, and Richard Yu was photographed carrying what looks like the Mate X8 in light purple (Gizmochina). But a NetEase report says the November timing is a mistake and the window is December, noting no blind orders or reservations have opened. Huawei has not announced a date, so it stays a Rumor. Update Nov 16: Huawei officially set the Mate X8 launch event for Nov 24 at 2:30 PM China time, matching the tipped date, and the teaser shows the purple color. The November timing is now Confirmed; the chip, screen and battery claims will be checked at the event, and we will resolve this after Nov 24.

items.title: Exynos Galaxy S27 models get a more efficient M2700 modem
items.claim: Exynos versions of the Galaxy S27 will use a new 4nm Samsung M2700 modem with Release 18 support, better satellite connectivity and idle power use on par with rivals; the Galaxy S28 follows with a 2nm M2800.
items.why: Reported by Korean outlet The Elec from an unnamed source, relayed by Android Authority and SamMobile. The Elec has a decent supply-chain record, but no performance figures were given and Samsung has not commented.

items.title: Xiaomi 18 Pro and Pro Max cost EUR 1,449-1,849 in Europe with smaller batteries
items.claim: The European Xiaomi 18 Pro will cost EUR 1,449 (256GB) or EUR 1,649 (512GB) with a 6,000mAh-rated battery and 90W charging, and the 18 Pro Max EUR 1,849 (512GB) with a 7,050mAh-rated battery and 100W, both smaller than the Chinese versions' 7,000mAh and 8,500mAh.
items.why: Prices first came from a single unnamed report relayed by GSMArena, and the battery figures matched Xiaomi's published EU energy labels. Update Oct 26: Italian retailer Epto listed both phones with the same smaller batteries (6,000mAh/90W on the Pro, 7,050mAh/100W on the Pro Max) and prices close to the leak: EUR 1,398.90 and 1,591.90 for the 18 Pro (256GB/512GB) and EUR 1,783.90 for the 18 Pro Max, about EUR 50-65 under the leaked figures. Epto's prices are often slightly off the official ones, so we move this to Likely: the batteries look settled, the price range is roughly right, but the exact euro figures and launch date still await Xiaomi. Update Nov 2: Xiaomi confirmed on X that the 18 Pro series goes global this November, which fits the retailer timing; prices and battery sizes are still unconfirmed until the launch event. Update Nov 9-10: Xiaomi set the global launch for Nov 17 in Paris, so the European prices and battery sizes will be checked then. Update Nov 17: after the Paris launch, Xiaomi's global and French product pages confirm the battery half of the claim: 6,000mAh with 90W on the 18 Pro and 7,050mAh with 100W on the 18 Pro Max. Official euro prices were not yet in the sources we checked, so it stays Likely until prices can be compared; a newer Dealabs leak put them EUR 50 lower than this claim (EUR 1,399/1,599 for the Pro, 1,599/1,799 for the Pro Max). Update Nov 18: official euro prices are now out: EUR 1,399 and 1,599 for the 18 Pro (256GB/512GB) and EUR 1,599, 1,799 and 2,099 for the 18 Pro Max (256GB/512GB/1TB), as reported by Gadgets360, Tweakers and MobiDevices. Each matching configuration is EUR 50 below this claim, and there is a cheaper 256GB Pro Max the claim did not include.
items.outcome: Partly correct. The smaller global batteries were exactly right (6,000mAh/90W and 7,050mAh/100W), but every price in the claim was EUR 50 too high: the 18 Pro costs EUR 1,399/1,599 and the 18 Pro Max EUR 1,799 for 512GB, with a EUR 1,599 256GB Pro Max and a EUR 2,099 1TB model the leak did not mention. The later Dealabs leak had the prices right.

items.title: Qualcomm launches two flagship Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 chips
items.claim: Qualcomm will unveil two Gen 6 flagship chips at Snapdragon Summit rather than one.
items.why: Qualcomm teased 'Dual 8 Elites' on Aug 19 and announced the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 and 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 on Sep 22. One detail was off: leaks called the second chip 'Pro', but Qualcomm named it 'Extreme'.
items.outcome: Confirmed, with a different name than leaked.

items.title: Pixel 11 prices go up $100
items.claim: Google's Pixel 11 would start at $899 and the Pro at $1,099, about $100 more than last year, after leaks of higher European prices.
items.why: Ars Technica extrapolated from European leaks; Google then priced the Pixel 11, Pro and Pro XL at $899, $1,099 and $1,299 on Aug 12.
items.outcome: Confirmed at launch.

items.title: NVIDIA has stopped making the RTX 5090
items.claim: NVIDIA has halted production of the GeForce RTX 5090 and is redirecting the GB202 chip to its professional RTX Pro cards.
items.why: Real signs pointed that way: Micro Center reclassified the card 'Not Carried', many stores sold out, and NVIDIA pulled it from its own marketplace. But on Oct 16 NVIDIA's head of personal computing, Jeff Fisher, told reporters in Taipei the RTX 5090 is not end-of-life and NVIDIA will keep shipping it, while admitting supply is tight. By Oct 17 the card was listed again on NVIDIA's US store, though not in stock.
items.outcome: Debunked by NVIDIA: the RTX 5090 has not been discontinued, though it remains scarce and expensive.

items.title: iPhone Duo 2 gets under-display Face ID
items.claim: Apple's second-generation iPhone Duo, expected next fall, adds Face ID under the outer display, and Apple is also considering an Action button.
items.why: From Bloomberg's Mark Gurman on his Power On podcast, relayed by MacRumors and 9to5Mac. Gurman has a strong Apple record, but he says Apple is only testing Face ID on prototypes and has not decided whether it will ship, so this stays a Rumor. The first iPhone Duo uses Touch ID in the side button. Early iPhone Duo reviews criticized the Touch ID placement, which makes Face ID a likely priority, but there is still no second source beyond Gurman. Update Nov 15: Gurman says Apple has built iPhone Duo 2 prototypes with Face ID in the outer display and calls it a top priority, but Apple is 'running out of time' for next fall's model and the feature may slip to the iPhone Duo 3. That makes it no more likely than before, so it stays a Rumor. Update Nov 18: Digital Chat Station says iPhone Duo 2 engineering units still have the 7.6-inch inner and 5.4-inch outer screens and a side fingerprint sensor, with no clear sign of Face ID (MacRumors). That is a second, independent source pointing against Face ID on next year's model, so this drops to Shaky.

items.title: Huawei adds a Pura 90 Plus with a 1-inch variable-aperture camera
items.claim: Huawei is preparing a Pura 90 Plus with a 50MP 1-inch-type RYYB variable-aperture main camera in a triple setup, a 6.8-inch 1.5K screen and four colors.
items.why: The phone itself is now official: on Oct 23 Huawei opened Pura 90 Plus pre-orders in China for an Oct 28 sale and showed four colors (matching the tipster's 'four colors') and up to 12GB/1TB. The camera and screen specs still come only from Weibo tipster Digital Chat Station, who has a decent record on Chinese phones, and Huawei has not published them. On Oct 25 live images of store display units showed a 2848x1276 (1.5K-class) screen and the Kirin 9025, matching the tipster's screen claim; the 1-inch variable-aperture camera is still unconfirmed. We will resolve this on Oct 28. Update Oct 28: Huawei launched the Pura 90 Plus with a 50MP 1-inch-type main camera with an f/1.4-4.0 variable aperture (RYYB, per Sina), a triple rear camera, a 6.8-inch 2848x1276 LTPO screen and four colors.
items.outcome: True. Huawei launched the Pura 90 Plus on Oct 28 with a 50MP 1-inch-type variable-aperture main camera in a triple camera setup, a 6.8-inch 1.5K-class screen and four colors, matching every part of the claim.

items.title: Samsung's China-only W27 is a premium Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra
items.claim: Samsung will release a W27 in China, a more premium Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra in blue with gold accents.
items.why: Samsung has now confirmed on Weibo a China launch on Oct 29 for a gold-framed book-style foldable, and its linked page mentions 'W2026' and the W series. That makes a W-series Fold 8 Ultra variant very likely, but Samsung has not used the W27 name or confirmed specs; Ice Universe says it matches the Z Fold 8 Ultra. We will resolve this on Oct 29. Update Oct 28: Evan Blass, who has a strong record, posted official-looking renders on Oct 27 showing a dark blue Fold 8-style phone with gold accents and the W-series gold logo. Samsung still has not named it; launch is Oct 29. Update Oct 29: Samsung launched the W27 in China, based on the Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra with a gold-finished frame, in blue and red, from 18,999 yuan.
items.outcome: True. Samsung launched the China-only W27 on Oct 29 as a premium Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra with gold accents and a blue color, as claimed. It also comes in red, which the leak did not mention.

items.title: Apple weighs a future iPhone Duo with a roughly 8-inch inner screen
items.claim: Apple is looking at a future iPhone Duo whose inner display is about half an inch larger (roughly 7.9 to 8.1 inches, versus 7.6 today), replacing rather than joining the current size.
items.why: Bloomberg's Mark Gurman said on his Power On podcast that he 'heard' Apple is 'looking at' the idea; he did not know the exact size and said it would not be a separate 'Max' model. Gurman's Apple record is strong, but this is an idea under consideration, not a product decision, so it could easily never ship.

items.title: Valve is working on a new Half-Life game codenamed 'HLX'
items.claim: 'HLX', a codename first found in 2024 game files, is an active Valve project, widely assumed to be a new Half-Life game.
items.why: On Oct 22 Valve composer Mike Morasky mentioned 'HLX has its own version' of Valve's audio HDR system during a GameSoundCon panel, and a co-panelist's reaction suggested it was a slip. That is the first time a Valve employee has said the name publicly, so the project likely exists, but nothing confirms it is a game, let alone Half-Life 3, or when it might be announced. Half-Life rumors have a long record of not panning out.

items.title: Honor 700 series launches in November with three models and a rear screen on every model
items.claim: Honor will launch three Honor 700 models in China in November; every model has a built-in rear display, and the 700 Pro adds a stronger camera setup around a roughly 9,000mAh battery class.
items.why: From Weibo tipsters relayed by GSMArena: one says the event is next month and the series has three models; Digital Chat Station has repeated the 200MP camera and rear screen since August. The timing fits Honor's six-month number-series cadence (the 600 launched in May), but Honor has announced nothing. On Oct 24 Digital Chat Station added details he says come from an engineering prototype (codename 'Flora'): a roughly 9,000mAh battery, a 50MP periscope on the Pro and four test colors, while calling the November timing tentative. More detail from the same tipster, so it stays a Rumor. Update Oct 28-Nov 1: two Honor 700 models (FAS-AN00 and FAA-AN00, thought to be the 700 and 700 Pro) passed China's 3C certification, with a tipster saying a third is pending, which usually means a launch within weeks. Tipster Dingjiao Shuma (via Kuai Keji, Oct 31) says the series launches in early November with actress Ju Jingyi as spokesperson, a Snapdragon chip, a periscope and support for a 200mm teleconverter. Certification plus several tipsters agreeing lifts the November timing to Likely; the 9,000mAh battery and exact specs still rest mainly on Digital Chat Station, and Honor has not announced a date. Update Nov 3: Honor CMO Guan Haitao officially announced the Honor 700 series on Weibo, confirmed the 'Flora' codename and said it debuts 'in winter', without a date. Tipster Wangzai Baishitong says the three models (700, 700 Pro and a Vitality Edition) launch this month. The series is now official; the November date and specs are still unconfirmed, so it stays Likely. Update Nov 3: Honor's global CMO Guan Haitao officially announced the Honor 700 series (codename Flora) for a 'winter' debut, and Honor named actress Ju Jingyi as ambassador. A tipster says three models (700, 700 Pro, and a Vitality Edition) are 3C certified and launch this month. Honor still has not given a date, so the November timing stays Likely. Update Nov 6: Honor officially revealed the Honor 700, 700 Pro and 700S with a rear display across the lineup and opened multi-channel pre-orders in China (colors Cold White, Clear Sky, Blue Tone, Pink Mist; memory configs listed on deposit pages). A launch-event date and final prices are still TBA, so the product itself is Confirmed while the exact on-sale day remains open. Camera, battery and chipset figures are still mostly tipster-led. Update Nov 9: a new Honor teaser shows heart-rate and blood-oxygen readings on the rear screen (GSMArena); Honor has not explicitly confirmed health sensing, and Digital Chat Station says the rear display also works as a selfie viewfinder and for notifications and mini games. Launch date still TBA. Update Nov 10: Honor set the launch for Nov 13 in a Weibo teaser (Notebookcheck, Huawei Central). The November timing and rear screens are now official; the camera and battery claims will be checked at the event. Update Nov 11: a Geekbench 6 listing for FAP-AN00, most likely the 700 Pro, shows a Snapdragon 8 Gen 5 with 16GB of RAM on Android 17, backing the leaked Pro chipset. Update Nov 13: the event moved to Nov 23 (2:30 PM, Wuhan), per Honor CEO Li Jian, so the launch is still in November. A China Telecom listing confirms the rear screen on all three, the 9,000mAh battery, the chipsets and the 200MP main camera, so the spec claims are now backed by a carrier database. We will resolve this after the Nov 23 event.

items.title: vivo S70 launches soon with a 64MP periscope that supports a teleconverter
items.expected: Not announced (China; S70 and S70 Pro reportedly together)
items.claim: vivo's next S-series phone, the S70, has a 64MP Sony LYT-610 periscope telephoto with support for a 200mm teleconverter, a 6.59-inch 1.5K LTPS OLED screen and the Snapdragon 8s Gen 4.
items.why: From tipster Digital Chat Station on Weibo, relayed by GSMArena; he says it is based on an engineering sample and that vivo tested, then dropped, a rear screen. DCS has a good record on Chinese phones, but this is a single source and vivo has said nothing. The S60 launched in May, so a late-2026 successor fits vivo's cadence. Update Oct 30: DCS added more detail, relayed by Gizmochina: the Snapdragon 8s Gen 4, a 50MP main, 8MP ultrawide and 50MP selfie camera, and support for a 200mm teleconverter. It is still the same single tipster, and reports point to a November launch in China. Update Nov 9: Digital Chat Station's latest leak (via 91mobiles and My Mobile India) adds an S70 Pro alongside the S70: both reportedly use the Snapdragon 8s Gen 4 and a 6.59-inch 1.5K 144Hz OLED, the S70 with up to an 8,000mAh battery and the Pro with a 200MP main camera, 64MP periscope and 7,000mAh-plus battery, both with 90W charging. 91mobiles says the Pro may go global as the V90 Pro. Still one tipster and no word from vivo, so it stays a Rumor.

items.title: Realme 17 Pro series gets a 10,000mAh battery, 200MP camera and 3.5x telephoto
items.expected: Unknown (the 16 Pro series launched in January)
items.claim: An upcoming Realme 17 Pro or 17 Pro+ has a flat 1.5K 120Hz OLED (165Hz in some games), the Dimensity 7500, a 200MP main camera, a 50MP 3.5x telephoto, a 10,000mAh battery and a plastic frame.
items.why: From a single tipster on X, relayed by GSMArena, which notes it is unclear whether this is the Pro or the Pro+. Realme has announced nothing; the leak is plausible given rivals' move to 10,000mAh batteries, but unverified. Update Nov 7: a new report citing industry sources (via GSMArena) gives the plain 17 Pro a 1.5K 120Hz AMOLED, Dimensity 7300, 50MP main and 8MP ultrawide cameras, IP68/IP69 and the same 10,000mAh battery. That suggests the earlier 200MP/3.5x-telephoto leak describes the Pro+ or Pro Max. The 10,000mAh battery now has two sources; the camera specs depend on which model.

items.title: OpenAI releases a cheaper GPT-6.1 Terra model that beats GPT-6.1 Sol
items.claim: OpenAI is about to release GPT-6.1 Terra, a new model in its Terra tier that outperforms GPT-6.1 Sol while costing less.
items.why: Two separate signals: a Microsoft pull request switched 18 evaluation configs from GPT-5.6 Terra to GPT-6.1 Terra, and The Information reported a new Terra model is coming. The model's existence is well supported, but the 'better than Sol for less' part comes only from The Information's paywalled report, and its reporter said some launches may slip into November. OpenAI has said nothing. Update Oct 26-27: OpenAI announced GPT-6.1 Terra on Oct 26. It is available to Plus, Pro, Enterprise and Edu users and in the API as gpt-6.1-terra at $1 per million input and $5 per million output tokens, 50% below GPT-6.1 Sol. OpenAI pitches it on computer use, saying it is over three times faster than Sol and GPT-6 Astra on its task benchmark, nearly matches them on MMMU-Pro and surpasses Sol on Terminal-Bench-Science, but recommends Sol or Astra for the most complex coding.
items.outcome: Mostly true. OpenAI released GPT-6.1 Terra on Oct 26 in ChatGPT Work, Codex and the API at half the API price of GPT-6.1 Sol. OpenAI's own benchmarks show it beating Sol on some tests (Terminal-Bench-Science) and nearly matching it on others, but OpenAI says Sol remains the better pick for the hardest coding work, so 'beats Sol' was only partly right.

items.title: Google releases Gemini 4 Carbon, the successor to Argon, within weeks
items.claim: Google's next Gemini 4 checkpoint, Carbon, is in partner early access and will be released publicly soon.
items.why: Business Insider first reported Carbon inside Google's internal coding tool, The Information said it is coming this month, testers report it on LMArena under Google's early access program, and Carbon 'teamfood' model IDs showed up in a Google server archive. That is strong evidence it exists and is close, but Google has not announced it and the date could slip into November. Early testers say it is better than Argon at 3D work but much slower. Update Oct 29: Google announced Gemini 4 Carbon on Oct 28, confirming it is real and in early access, but only for selected cyber defenders. Public access for developers and consumers is promised 'as soon as possible' with no date, so we keep this open until it is broadly available. Update Nov 4: a week after the announcement, Carbon is still limited to cyber defenders and Fairwind partners. The Gemini API changelog lists Argon (GA Oct 13) but no Carbon model ID, and Google has given no date for developers or consumers. Argon reached the public 13 days after its announcement, but that is not a promise for Carbon. Update Nov 10: Carbon reached the Gemini app, AI Mode and Antigravity for AI Ultra subscribers and the Gemini API paid tier (9to5Google).
items.outcome: Correct. Carbon was real and went public within weeks: announced Oct 28 for cyber defenders, then opened to AI Ultra subscribers and paid API developers on Nov 10, three weeks after the first reports. It launched for paying tiers, not free users.

items.title: Xbox turns Game Pass into a pick-your-features subscription
items.claim: Microsoft will overhaul Game Pass into a tiered base plan with à la carte add-ons for console-only games, cloud gaming and multiplayer.
items.why: Reported by Fortune from people familiar with the plans and relayed by GameSpot, Engadget and others. It fits an April report of a 'pick-your-own' Game Pass and CEO Asha Sharma's public goal of a 'more flexible system', but there is no timing, pricing or official confirmation, and the same Fortune story's other claims (the $1,200-1,800 next Xbox) are tracked separately.

items.title: Samsung readies a Galaxy Fit 4 that looks just like the Fit 3
items.claim: Samsung will launch a Galaxy Fit 4 (SM-R391) fitness band with a near-identical design to the Fit 3, in black, white and light blue, at a similar low price.
items.why: Android Authority obtained 360-degree videos of the band in three colors and earlier found Samsung documents naming SM-R391 as 'FIT4'; a Samsung app teardown also showed renders. The hardware is well evidenced, but specs beyond Bluetooth LE and a Goodix optical sensor, the price (the Fit 3 was about $60) and the launch date are unknown; reports range from late 2026 to early 2027. Update Oct 30: a SammyGuru teardown of the Galaxy Fit 4 Manager app, reported by Android Authority, lists nearly the same health features as the Fit 3 (sleep coaching, SpO2, snoring detection, auto workout tracking), the same tile-based UI with up to 12 tiles, and 258 x 428 watch-face assets that suggest a slightly taller screen. Update Oct 31: GSMArena, citing the same SammyGuru teardown, reads the watch-face colors as black, silver and light green cases and found no sign of GPS. Still no launch date or price from Samsung. Update Nov 5: SamMobile found a Wallet section in the leaked Galaxy Fit 4 Manager plugin, pointing to NFC payments through Samsung Wallet (a first for the Fit line), plus Modes and Routines support, photo watch faces and what looks like a speaker for calls. Samsung still has not announced it.

items.title: Samsung's Exynos 2700 beats Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 phones in internal tests
items.claim: In Samsung's internal tests the Exynos 2700 for the Galaxy S27 beat the Xiaomi 18 Pro Max (Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6) by about 20% in Geekbench 6.5 multi-core and posted 5-20% higher GPU results.
items.why: A single report from Korea's Chosun Biz, relayed by Android Authority. It covers only multi-core CPU and unnamed peak GPU tests against one Xiaomi phone, with nothing on single-core speed, sustained performance, heat or battery life, and the numbers come from Samsung's own testing. A 10-core Exynos winning multi-core against an 8-core chip is plausible, but the headline 'beats Snapdragon' needs independent benchmarks.

items.title: Samsung cuts Galaxy A phone production by about 20% to protect flagships
items.claim: Samsung has cut fourth-quarter Galaxy A component orders by about 20% versus its plan, about 10 million phones a year, and plans to cut Galaxy A output by more than 10% again in 2027, shifting resources to flagships as memory costs soar.
items.why: Reported by Korea's ETNews and relayed by 9to5Google; Samsung has not commented. It fits the wider memory-price squeeze: ETNews says memory and chips now make up about half of a mid-range phone's cost and that Samsung's mobile division is losing money this year. But it rests on one outlet's supply-chain sourcing, and production plans are hard to verify from outside.

items.title: BYD's Yangwang Altior luxury sedan debuts in the UAE in early November with solid-state batteries
items.claim: BYD will unveil its 5.5-meter Yangwang Altior executive sedan in Dubai around Nov 5, as the first car with BYD's solid-state batteries, priced around 2 million yuan.
items.why: The name is official: on Oct 27 BYD revealed the sedan as the Yangwang Altior (DingYao in China) with a teaser, and Yangwang's Hu Xiaoqing had already said the global launch will be in the UAE. The Nov 5 date comes from CarNewsChina citing people familiar with the project; BYD has not announced a date. The solid-state battery and the roughly 2 million yuan price are reports only, and BYD's Stella Li has said its first solid-state car debuts in 2027, so that part is the weakest. Rear-hinged coach doors are visible in teasers and prototype photos. Update Oct 30: Hu Xiaoqing confirmed the Altior has rear-hinged (suicide) doors, a first for BYD, and previewed a dot-matrix grille; a teaser shows it at a BYD Flash Charging station. BYD still has not confirmed the Nov 5 date or a solid-state pack. Update Nov 2: several outlets now print Nov 5 as the Dubai debut date, but they trace back to the same CarNewsChina report; BYD still has not published a date or battery chemistry. We will resolve this after Nov 5. Update Nov 5: BYD's own teaser now sets the debut for Nov 8 in Abu Dhabi, not Nov 5 in Dubai, so the reported date was a few days off. Uncamouflaged prototypes show a large chrome grille, rear-hinged doors and roof LiDAR. BYD still has not mentioned solid-state batteries or a price, so the rating stays Rumor until the Nov 8 reveal. Update Nov 6: Still on track for the Nov 8 Abu Dhabi debut per BYD's Nov 5 teaser and CarNewsChina; no new official word on solid-state batteries or pricing, so the rating stays Rumor until the reveal. Update Nov 8: BYD's official press release and multiple reports confirm the Altior debuted in Abu Dhabi on Nov 7. It is a 5.6-meter four-seat EV with coach doors, a second-generation Blade Battery and more than 1,000 km of CLTC range. The Shanhe Dingyun limited edition opened pre-orders at 2.08 million yuan. Official materials do not mention solid-state batteries.
items.outcome: Mixed. Yangwang unveiled the Altior in Abu Dhabi on Nov 7 (not Dubai around Nov 5 as first reported; BYD later teased Nov 8). It is a 5.6-meter four-seat luxury EV with coach doors, and the Shanhe Dingyun limited edition opened pre-orders at 2.08 million yuan, close to the rumored 2 million yuan. The solid-state battery claim did not hold: BYD's official materials specify a second-generation Blade Battery with more than 1,000 km of CLTC range.

items.title: Oppo Find X10 Ultra gets a LOFIC 200MP main camera, two periscopes and a 100MP selfie camera
items.claim: The Find X10 Ultra will have a 200MP 1/1.12-inch main camera with LOFIC, a 200MP periscope, a 50MP 10x periscope and a 100MP square-sensor selfie camera.
items.why: From Weibo tipster Digital Chat Station, who has a decent record on Oppo, relayed by GSMArena. By the leak's own account two sensors (the 200MP periscope and the 10x periscope) are not finalized, and the 10x camera could fall back to a smaller 1/2.76-inch sensor if the preferred 1/1.95-inch part is delayed. The phone is months away and Oppo has said nothing. Update Nov 5: leaker Yogesh Brar (via Android Authority) gives a different setup: 200MP main, 200MP ultrawide, 200MP 3x periscope and 50MP 10x periscope. That conflicts with Digital Chat Station's 50MP-class ultrawide, so the main camera and two periscopes look consistent across tipsters while the ultrawide is disputed. Update Nov 6: Digital Chat Station now says the Find X10 Ultra project has been suspended (see the separate cancellation rumor). If true, these specs never ship; Oppo has not commented.

items.title: Motorola Edge 70 Neo has a Snapdragon 7s Gen 3, 7,000mAh battery and 144Hz screen
items.claim: The Edge 70 Neo will have a 6.78-inch 144Hz AMOLED, Snapdragon 7s Gen 3, 50MP Sony LYTIA 710 main camera, 32MP selfie camera, 7,000mAh battery with 45W charging and IP64.
items.why: The phone itself is real: Motorola accidentally teased it in August and renders followed. The spec list comes from a single leak reported by GSMArena with no certification or official backing yet. Motorola has not announced a launch date. Update Nov 18: Motorola's Flipkart teaser sets an India launch for Nov 24 and shows '50MP', 'OIS' and 'Lytia' on the camera ring, matching the leaked 50MP Lytia main camera (earlier renders showed 200MP). The chip, battery and screen are still unconfirmed, so it stays a Rumor until the launch. Update Nov 19: Motorola has now confirmed the Snapdragon 7s Gen 3, a 6.8-inch 144Hz AMOLED, the 50MP Lytia 710 main camera, a 7,000mAh battery with 45W charging and IP64, matching the leak. Only the 32MP selfie camera is unconfirmed; we will resolve this after the Nov 24 launch.

items.title: Bloober Team's Silent Hill remake targets a 2027 release
items.claim: Bloober Team's remake of the first Silent Hill, cast under the codename 'Project Noise', is aiming for a 2027 release.
items.why: Konami announced the remake in mid-2025, about eight months after Bloober's well-received Silent Hill 2 remake, but has given no date. The 2027 window and the first two cast names come from a single MP1st report, which VGC and IGN have relayed; MP1st itself says it is an internal target that can move.

items.title: iPhone 18e keeps a 60Hz screen but gets the A20 and possibly a 24MP selfie camera
items.claim: The iPhone 18e will have a 6.12-inch 60Hz LTPS OLED screen, the 2nm A20 chip, a single 48MP rear camera and maybe a 24MP front camera.
items.why: From Weibo tipster Digital Chat Station, relayed by MacRumors and Android Authority. The 60Hz display repeats this leaker's earlier claim and fits Apple's pattern for the 16e and 17e, and the A20 matches what is expected for the standard iPhone 18. The leaker hedged on the front camera, and MacRumors notes 24MP may be a mix-up with the 18MP Center Stage camera. Apple has not announced the phone. Update Nov 4: a second Weibo leaker, Fixed Focus Digital, says a new chip is the only upgrade they can confirm so far and hints the notch may stay. That agrees on the chip but adds nothing on the screen or cameras. Update Nov 15: Fixed Focus Digital now says (Nov 9, via GSMArena and 91mobiles) the 18e gets a 6.3-inch 60Hz OLED, the same size as the iPhone 18, plus the same 4,430 mAh battery and a single 48MP camera. That directly contradicts Digital Chat Station's 6.12-inch claim, so this is re-rated Shaky until the screen size settles; the 60Hz panel, A20-class chip and single 48MP camera are where the leakers agree.

items.title: Samsung adds a Galaxy Z Fold 9 Plus or Fold 9 FE next to the wide Fold 9
items.claim: Samsung is testing two extra wide-format Fold 9 variants, a larger 'Plus' and a cheaper, spec-trimmed 'FE', and will pick one to sell alongside the Galaxy Z Fold 9.
items.why: A single leaker, Lanzuk (yeux1122) on Naver, citing unnamed display supply-chain sources. The leaker says Samsung will choose only one of the two and the plan is in early testing, so it could easily change before mid-2027. Samsung has not commented.

items.title: Motorola Signature 27 costs about €1,595 in Europe, and a Razr Flex 27 about €1,511
items.expected: Signature 27: Nov 16 in Europe (announced); Razr Flex 27 not announced
items.claim: The Motorola Signature 27 (12GB/512GB) will cost €1,594.90 in Europe, up nearly 60% from the first Signature's €999, and the unannounced Razr Flex 27 (12GB/256GB) will cost €1,510.90.
items.why: The prices come from listings on Portuguese retailer MegaPC. Retailer listings are real evidence but often use placeholder prices: the Razr Flex listings have no photos, one wrongly describes a clamshell, and all are out of stock with no ship date. Motorola has not confirmed European or US pricing. Update Oct 29: Motorola's US and India pages say the Signature 27 arrives in November, which fits the retailer timing, but it still has not confirmed any price. Update Nov 5: Motorola announced the Signature 27 with a recommended European price of EUR 1,899, not EUR 1,595, going on sale Nov 16; GSMArena says some retailers and partners will sell it at EUR 1,399. The US price is $1,599. The Razr Flex 27 is still unannounced.
items.outcome: Wrong. The leaked EUR 1,594.90 retailer price matched neither of Motorola's figures: the official recommended price is EUR 1,899, with some partners at EUR 1,399. The 'nearly 60% more than the first Signature' framing understated the official jump. The Razr Flex 27 price remains unverifiable because the phone has not been announced.

items.title: vivo is testing an X500s with a 6.85-inch flat 2K 144Hz screen
items.expected: Possibly with the X500 Ultra, rumored for Mar-Apr 2027 (China)
items.claim: vivo has a 'small s iteration' of the X500 series in testing with a 6.85-inch flat screen, 2K+ resolution, 144Hz and equal bezels, likely the X500s.
items.why: Weibo tipster Digital Chat Station, who has a good record on Chinese phones, described the engineering sample but did not name it; the X500s label is readers' and GSMArena's inference. The X300s launched with the X300 Ultra in March, so a spring 2027 debut alongside the X500 Ultra is a guess based on that pattern.

items.title: Apple relaxed iPhone Duo quality checks to ship more units
items.claim: Apple lowered quality inspection standards for the iPhone Duo to get more units to stores before the holidays, as it targets 7.5 million shipments by year end.
items.why: The claim comes from one unnamed Foxconn employee quoted by China's Jiemian News and relayed by GSMArena. Sina reports another supply-chain source who denies Apple lowered its yield standards, and the reports themselves say a batch of components was replaced. Apple has acknowledged inner-display damage on 'a small number' of units and offers replacements, but has said nothing about inspection standards. A single anonymous source with a direct denial makes this Shaky.

items.title: The base Galaxy S27 stays at 25W wired charging
items.claim: The standard Galaxy S27 will charge at 25W wired, the same as the Galaxy S26, while the S27 Pro and Ultra get 60W.
items.why: Hard evidence from certifications: a China 3C listing for model SM-S9520 last month showed 25W, and on Oct 29 GSMArena reported UL Solutions (Demko) certificates for several variants rated 9V/2.77A (24.93W). The 60W figure for the Pro and Ultra comes from separate 3C filings reported by smaller sites. Certifications are reliable on charging limits, but Samsung has not announced the phones.

items.title: Intel's Moon Lake replaces N-series chips in 2028 with four low-power cores
items.claim: Intel's next budget chip, Moon Lake, has four low-power efficiency cores and no performance cores, runs at 6-15W and replaces the N-series chips in cheap laptops and mini PCs in 2028.
items.why: From leaker Jaykihn, who has a decent record on Intel roadmaps, relayed by Tom's Hardware. It is a single source with no clock speeds, process or exact date, and Intel has said nothing about Moon Lake.

items.title: Samsung is developing a 17-inch tablet that folds down to 8 inches
items.claim: Samsung has started developing a foldable tablet with a 17-inch screen that folds into an 8-inch device, after testing several versions.
items.why: A single social-media post from tipster @kro_roe, relayed by SamMobile, which itself calls it far-fetched. There is no timeline, no detail on the design (a wrap-around screen or an inner screen plus cover screen) and no corroboration. Samsung Display has shown large foldable concepts for years without products following.

items.title: iPhone Air 2 gets a 6.55-inch 120Hz screen, A20 chip and two 48MP rear cameras
items.claim: The iPhone Air 2 launches next spring with a 6.55-inch flat 120Hz OLED, a 2nm A20-series chip, 48MP wide and 48MP ultrawide rear cameras and a bigger battery than the first Air.
items.why: From tipster Digital Chat Station, relayed by GSMArena; it repeats earlier leaks of a second rear camera and a spring launch. DCS is reliable on Chinese phones but less proven on Apple, and the 5.2mm thickness and battery figures come from other, separate leaks. Apple has said nothing. Update Nov 10: tipster Smart Pikachu posted alleged iPhone Air 2 dummy units on Weibo showing two rear cameras and a slimmer body. Dummies are usually built from leaked CAD files, so they back the design but not the chip or screen specs. Update Nov 18: Korea's ETNews reports the Air 2 keeps the first Air's display specs so Apple can use existing OLED inventory, with Samsung Display the only supplier and panel production starting in late December or early January for a March launch (MacRumors). That supports the spring timing and an unchanged screen, but says nothing about the chip or cameras, so it stays a Rumor. Update Nov 20: Sonny Dickson posted new dummy units of the Air 2 and iPhone 18 showing two horizontally placed rear cameras on the Air's wide plateau (MacRumors). It is more support for the dual-camera design only; chip, screen and battery claims are unchanged, so it stays a Rumor.

items.title: Samsung's Android XR glasses go on sale in mid-December, in Korea and the US only
items.expected: Ships Dec 10, 2026 (US and South Korea, official)
items.claim: Samsung's display-free Intelligent Eyewear (Android XR, Gemini, Snapdragon AR1 Gen 1) goes on sale in mid-December in South Korea and the US first, with Europe, China and Japan later; pricing is not set.
items.why: From a Korean media report relayed by GSMArena. It fits an earlier Korean report quoting a Samsung official on a November launch, and Samsung's playbook for the Galaxy XR headset (Korea and US first). Samsung has shown the glasses and their Gentle Monster and Warby Parker frames but has not given a date or price. Update Nov 3: Android Authority relays the same Chosun Biz report (mid-December, Korea and US first, 'Intelligent Eyewear' name, other markets in 2027). That is wider coverage of one report, not a second source, so it stays a Rumor. Update Nov 6: Gentle Monster, one of the two frame partners, said on X that its Intelligent Eyewear collection launches in December, and Warby Parker opens US pre-orders on Nov 12. The December window is now official, so this moves to Likely; the exact mid-December timing and the Korea/US-only first wave still rest on the Chosun Biz report. Update Nov 12: Samsung, Google and the frame partners opened pre-orders in the US and South Korea only, from $395, with retail availability on Dec 10.
items.outcome: Mostly correct. The glasses ship on Dec 10, which is early-to-mid December rather than squarely mid-month, and the first wave is the US and South Korea as reported. Pricing, which the report said was not set, starts at $395.

items.title: Galaxy Z Fold9 brings back an under-display selfie camera
items.claim: Samsung's next book-style foldable returns to an under-display camera on the inner screen, with major internal changes but little change in thickness, positioned against the iPhone Duo.
items.why: One tipster on X, relayed by GSMArena. The same source earlier claimed 3.9mm unfolded and 7.9mm folded, which clashes with 'minimal thickness changes' given the current wide Fold8 is 4.5mm and 9.7mm, and it is unclear which Fold9 model is meant. Samsung used under-display cameras from the Fold3 to Fold6, so it is technically plausible, but the sourcing is thin and internally inconsistent.

items.title: Oppo Find X10 Ultra switches to MediaTek's Dimensity 9600 Pro
items.claim: The Find X10 Ultra (model PYU110, codename 'Xinyun') uses MediaTek's Dimensity 9600 Pro instead of a Snapdragon chip.
items.why: Tipster Abhishek Yadav on X and Weibo's Smart Pikachu both pointed to the Dimensity 9600 Pro, which Oppo already uses in the Find X10 Pro Max. But Smart Pikachu has since said a Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 version is now more likely, per Android Central's summary via Gadget Hacks. Conflicting signals from the same small pool of leakers; Oppo has not confirmed the phone exists. Update Nov 6: Digital Chat Station now says the Find X10 Ultra project has been suspended (see the separate cancellation rumor). If true, these specs never ship; Oppo has not commented.

items.title: HMD readies '2nd Edition' refreshes of the Pulse Pro, Fusion and Crest Max
