items.claim: HMD will sell a Pulse Pro 2nd Edition with a 120Hz screen, MediaTek Helio G99, 8GB RAM and 256GB storage for about THB 4,990 (around $148), and give the Fusion (Snapdragon 7s Gen 2) and Crest Max (Dimensity 7025) the same 2nd Edition treatment.
items.why: The Pulse Pro 2nd Edition showed up in a listing from what appears to be the official Nokia shop in Thailand, spotted by a tipster on X and relayed by GSMArena; the same tipster had leaked an EU version a week earlier. A retailer listing is strong evidence for the Pulse Pro refresh, so it is Likely. The Fusion and Crest Max 2nd Editions come only from the tipster, and HMD has announced nothing. Note that a Pulse 2 Pro was listed by a Swiss retailer in 2025 and never launched.

items.title: Atlus is remaking the first Persona game
items.claim: Leaked footage shows a remake of Revelations: Persona in development, built in Unreal Engine.
items.why: About two minutes of work-in-progress footage (field, battle and event scenes) was posted to YouTube on Oct 31 by a renamed account and quickly mirrored. Gematsu notes it resembles the sizzle reel that leaked before Persona 3 Reload, shows Unreal Engine debug text, and reuses a Persona summon animation from Persona 4 Revival, which adds credibility. Oddities: Persona 2's Tatsuya Suou appears in battle, perhaps as a stand-in. Atlus and Sega have not commented. Plausible leak with some supporting detail, but one source and unverified.

items.title: Galaxy S27 Pro and S27 Ultra get an upgraded Privacy Display; S27 and S27+ don't
items.claim: Samsung will put an improved version of the S26 Ultra's Privacy Display, plus brighter screens, on both the Galaxy S27 Pro and S27 Ultra, while the S27 and S27+ go without.
items.why: A SamMobile exclusive; SamMobile has good Samsung sourcing but this is one report with no detail on what the upgrade is. It would be the first time the feature reaches a non-Ultra model, and it fits other reports that the S27 Pro shares Ultra hardware (200MP main camera, 50MP ultrawide). The S27 Pro itself is still unannounced (see our four-model rumor, rated Likely).

items.title: Apple launches an OLED iPad Air, a vapor-chamber iPad Pro and an A19 base iPad in the first half of 2027
items.claim: Apple will release three iPads in the first half of 2027: an iPad Air with an OLED screen, an iPad Pro with a new chip and vapor-chamber cooling, and a base iPad with the A19, 8GB of RAM (enabling Apple Intelligence), the N1 wireless chip and the C1X modem.
items.why: From Bloomberg's Mark Gurman (Power On, Nov 1), who called this autumn's MacBook Pro, iPad mini and iMac line-up correctly. Chip choices beyond the base iPad's A19 (M5 for the Air, M6 or later for the Pro) are outlets' expectations, not part of the report. One strong source and no supply-chain confirmation yet, so it stays a Rumor. Update Nov 6: Korean industry sources (via GSMArena and SamMobile) independently put the first OLED iPad Air in the first half of 2027, with Samsung Display supplying most panels alongside BOE and 4-5 million Air units forecast for 2027. Supply-chain backing for the headline OLED Air moves this to Likely; the iPad Pro and base iPad details are still Gurman-only. Update Nov 10: DigiTimes (via MacRumors) also says both iPad Air sizes move to OLED in the first half of 2027, using the iPad mini's single-stack LTPS panel design (earlier DigiTimes reporting said it stays at 60Hz), with Samsung Display the main supplier and BOE still qualifying. Another supply-chain source for the OLED Air; stays Likely.

items.title: Second-generation touchscreen MacBook Pros get M7 Pro/Max in 2027, and non-touch Pro models are dropped
items.claim: Apple will ship second-generation OLED touchscreen MacBook Pros with M7 Pro and M7 Max chips next year and then stop selling the non-touch M5 Pro/Max models, keeping only an entry 14-inch MacBook Pro that moves to M7 and the new thinner design without touch.
items.why: From Mark Gurman's Nov 1 Power On newsletter, relayed by AppleInsider and Digital Trends; MacRumors earlier reported (Oct 15) that the OLED models won't get M7 until late 2027. Gurman's Mac reporting has been reliable this year, but this is a single source about plans a year out, and Apple has not commented. The current touchscreen models launched Oct 28 with M5 Pro/Max. Update Nov 4: MacRumors relays Gurman's view that Apple will likely fold its high-end MacBook Pros into touchscreen-only models, and repeats the 2027 M7 Pro/Max touch generation plus a thinner M7 base 14-inch. Same single source, so still Rumor.

items.title: Sony announces the PlayStation 6 in early March 2027
items.claim: Sony's current roadmap targets a PlayStation 6 announcement in early March 2027.
items.why: From PlayStation insider Millie A on X, who has a decent but mixed record, and who hedged it with 'as of today'. No second source. ComicBook reads it as pointing to a holiday 2027 release, which conflicts with Bloomberg-style reports that next-gen consoles may slip to 2028 or later (see our consoles-delay rumor); a reveal date says little on its own about launch timing. Sony has said nothing. Update Nov 3: the Millie A post is dated Oct 29; the wider coverage since then (IBTimes, regional outlets) all traces back to it, so there is still one source. Reconciled with our consoles-delay rumor: a March 2027 reveal could still precede a 2028 launch, so we treat the two as compatible and keep this a Rumor. Sony has not commented.

items.title: OnePlus 16T is a compact phone with a Dimensity 9600M and two 200MP cameras
items.claim: A compact Oppo-made phone will launch outside China as the OnePlus 16T with a 6.35-inch 1.5K 120Hz LTPO screen, MediaTek's 3nm Dimensity 9600M, a 200MP main camera and a 200MP periscope, a metal frame under 9mm and a battery of about 7,000mAh with 80W charging.
items.why: From Digital Chat Station on Weibo, relayed by tipster Debayan Roy and Gadgets360. The tipster has a good record on Chinese phones, but the OnePlus naming is his interpretation and neither OnePlus nor MediaTek (which has not announced a Dimensity 9600M) has said anything. The OnePlus 15T launched in China in March with Snapdragon and dual 50MP cameras, so the chip switch would be a notable change.

items.title: Galaxy A38 gets a 6,000mAh battery, the A30 series' first upgrade in six years
items.claim: The Galaxy A38's battery is rated at 5,882mAh, likely marketed as 6,000mAh, up from the 5,000mAh the A30 line has used since the Galaxy A31; charging likely stays at 45W.
items.why: From Dutch site Galaxy Club, which often reports Samsung battery ratings from certification and supply data, relayed by Android Authority and SamMobile. It fits reports of bigger batteries across Samsung's 2027 lineup. The 45W figure is an inference from the A37 and A58, not part of the leak. Samsung has said nothing.

items.title: Apple weighs cheaper high-mobility oxide (HMO) backplanes for future Mac OLED screens
items.claim: Apple is evaluating ways to mass-produce high-mobility oxide (HMO) TFT backplanes for future OLED panels, possibly as a successor to LTPO, with Samsung Display and LG Display favoring a cheaper sputtering process over atomic layer deposition.
items.why: From Korean outlet The Elec, relayed by MacRumors; analyst Ross Young says HMO is already used in the new touchscreen MacBook Pro. The Elec has good supply-chain sources but its timelines often slip, and the report names no product or date: MacBooks and iMacs are only listed as possible uses. Apple has said nothing.

items.title: Galaxy S27 Pro uses the regular Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6, not the Ultra's Extreme chip
items.claim: In Europe, the Galaxy S27 and S27+ use the Exynos 2700, the S27 Pro uses the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 (SM8950), and only the S27 Ultra gets the Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6, all with 12GB of RAM and 256GB of storage.
items.why: From import-export records on the NBD trade platform, found by Notebookcheck and relayed by SamMobile, GSMArena and Android Police. Shipping records with real model numbers (SM-S952B to SM-S958B) are hard evidence, so this is Likely, but they can reflect test units and Samsung has not announced the phones. The split mirrors Xiaomi's 18 Pro (regular chip) and 18 Pro Max (Extreme). Update Nov 6: yeux1122 (via GSMArena) adds that the Pro (Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6) and Ultra (Extreme Gen 6) use Snapdragon in South Korea too, while the S27 and S27+ stay on Exynos 2700 outside North America. Update Nov 20: a Geekbench listing for the SM-S957B, the Asia/Europe Galaxy S27 Pro, shows Samsung's Exynos 2700 (S5E9975) with an Xclipse 970 GPU and 12GB of RAM on Android 17 (SamMobile). That directly contradicts the Snapdragon claim for Europe. Both pieces of evidence are hard-looking, so with conflicting reports we downgrade this to Shaky until Samsung announces the phones.

items.title: Standard iPhone 18 gets a bigger battery and a higher price
items.expected: Spring 2027 (with iPhone 18e and iPhone Air 2, rumored)
items.claim: The standard iPhone 18 will have a larger battery than the iPhone 17's 3,692 mAh (reportedly 4,430 mAh), keep a 6.3-inch 120Hz OLED with Dynamic Island, use the 2nm A20 and dual 48MP cameras, and may cost more.
items.why: From Weibo leaker Digital Chat Station, relayed by MacRumors, The Verge and AppleInsider. DCS has a fair supply-chain record, and a battery bump fits Apple raising capacities on the iPhone 18 Pro. But no capacity was given, and the price part is the leaker's own speculation with no figure or market; Apple already raised the iPhone 17 to $899 in September. Apple has said nothing. Update Nov 15 (catching up on Nov 5-9 leaks): alleged X-ray images shared by leaker Littertree66 put the battery at 4,430 mAh, and Weibo tipster Fixed Focus Digital gave the same 4,430 mAh figure on Nov 9, adding that the physical SIM slot is dropped and the main sensor is physically smaller. Two leaks now agree on the capacity, but the higher price is still speculation, so the claim as a whole stays a Rumor.

items.title: Ubisoft bids to buy Arkane Lyon from Xbox
items.expected: Xbox's sale deadline is about mid-December (extended by a month from Nov 13)
items.claim: Ubisoft and at least two other game companies have made offers to buy Arkane Lyon, the studio making Marvel's Blade, and Xbox has also considered a management buyout.
items.why: Reported by Bloomberg, citing people familiar with the talks, and relayed by PC Gamer, The Verge and VGC. Bloomberg is reliable on deals, but this is one report, no deal is agreed, and neither Xbox nor Ubisoft has commented. The background is confirmed: Xbox is trying to divest Arkane and extended its search deadline by a month from Nov 13 to explore options for Blade.

items.title: Honor is testing a 14,000-15,000mAh phone battery for a week of use
items.claim: Honor has a 14,000-15,000mAh high-density phone battery in trial production, aimed at a phone that lasts about a week per charge without being unusually thick or heavy.
items.why: From Weibo tipster Digital Chat Station, relayed by GSMArena, Notebookcheck, Gizmochina and TechRadar. DCS correctly called Honor's earlier 12,000mAh-class cell before the Win RT 2 shipped with 12,070mAh, and Honor keeps raising capacities. Still a single leaker with no model, date or market, and the 'week of battery life' is a target, not a test result.

items.title: Galaxy A58 keeps 45W charging and ships without a charger in China
items.claim: The Galaxy A58 (SM-A5860) supports 45W wired charging, the same as the A57, and comes without a charger in the box in China.
items.why: From China's 3C certification, reported by GSMArena. Certification listings are hard evidence for charging specs, but Samsung has not announced the phone, and the launch window and battery size are not confirmed. Separate leaks claim the A58 keeps the A57's camera setup.

items.title: Galaxy Z Fold9 and Z Fold9 Ultra keep their predecessors' rear cameras
items.claim: Samsung's 2027 book-style foldables carry over their rear cameras: the Fold9 Ultra keeps a 200MP main, 50MP ultrawide and 3x telephoto, and the wide Fold9 keeps 50MP main and 50MP ultrawide cameras.
items.why: From Korean tipster Lanzuk, relayed by GSMArena, SamMobile and Android Police. Lanzuk has a decent record, including correctly calling video LUTs on the Fold8 Ultra. The claim fits Samsung's habit of reusing sensors, but it is one source and gives no telephoto resolution. See also our separate under-display selfie camera rumor.

items.title: Samsung readies Galaxy T1 ear-hook sports earbuds, including for the US
items.claim: Samsung will launch ear-hook fitness earbuds, model SM-R545 and codenamed Galaxy T1, in several markets including the US.
items.why: The earbuds passed the FCC on Nov 4 (IDs ZCASMR545L and ZCASMR545R, case EP-QR545) after certifications in China, South Korea and Indonesia, and the filings mention a 'T1 Project'. That is strong evidence a product is coming, as Android Authority reports. The retail name, price and early-2027 timing are not confirmed; earlier leaks of a 595mAh case and a fit test come from software code. Update Nov 19: SammyGuru found the earbuds in the One UI 9.5 beta under the name Galaxy Buds Active: in-ear with ear hooks, IP68, ANC, 360 Audio (no head tracking), up to 96kHz audio and Auracast, apparently without wear detection (Android Authority). Samsung's own software naming them makes the product even more certain, but price and date are still unknown, so it stays Likely. Update Nov 20: GSMArena adds that the One UI 9.5 code lists adjustable ANC, 96kHz Ultra High Quality audio, Auto Switch and a fit test, but no in-ear detection, and notes they appear in the same beta as the Galaxy Studio headphones expected with the S27. Still no date or price; stays Likely.

sources.name: Android Authority (Buds Active in One UI 9.5)

items.title: The Elder Scrolls VI: Sentinel is more than two years away
items.expected: 2029 or later (reported); Bethesda has given no date
items.claim: Bethesda's newly named The Elder Scrolls VI: Sentinel will not ship for more than two years.
items.why: Bethesda revealed the Sentinel subtitle on Nov 4 and said it will be 'some time' before it shares more. Bloomberg's Jason Schreier, who called Fallout 76 and Starfield timing correctly, then said the game is 'still more than two years away' and doubled down on Reddit; Windows Central's Jez Corden said the same. Two well-sourced reporters agreeing makes this Likely, though release windows this far out often move.

items.title: Apple's HomeView will run third-party AI chatbots like ChatGPT and Claude
items.expected: Not announced (code is in iOS 27.3 beta 1, not yet active)
items.claim: Apple's HomeView hub will allow third-party conversational AI apps such as ChatGPT and Claude.
items.why: Leaker pdfu found an unused ConversationalApps flag earlier this month and says iOS 27.3 beta 1 adds a Conversational Apps category to PebblePlay, HomeView's CarPlay-style app bridge, along with two-way audio routing and session handling (reported by 9to5Mac). Apple uses these category flags to decide which third-party apps can run, so this is hard evidence of intent. It is still 'not fully wired up', and Apple has not named any apps or a date. Update Nov 8: The Verge also covered the iOS 27.3 code and adds that the same beta brings anti-spoofing protection for HomeView: after three failed attempts the user must authenticate on an iPhone, with lockouts that grow from one hour to eight. Apple still has not announced either feature, so this stays Likely.

items.title: Apple asks suppliers for 16 million MacBook Neo laptops in 2027, double this year
items.claim: Apple has asked suppliers to build 16 million MacBook Neo laptops in 2027, about twice the volume expected for 2026.
items.why: From DigiTimes' supply chain sources, reported by MacRumors. DigiTimes is often right on direction but less reliable on exact numbers. It fits Bloomberg's September report of a second-generation Neo with an A19 Pro and 12GB of RAM in 2027 and Apple's record fiscal 2026 Mac sales, but Apple does not publish per-model numbers, so this is hard to verify.

items.title: Huawei's new sub-brand is called Osta and debuts with the flagship-level Osta O1 and wide-screen O1 Pro
items.claim: Huawei's upcoming sub-brand, reported in Chinese as Xingmang, will be called Osta in English and launch with two flagship-level phones: the Osta O1 with a quad-curved screen and the Osta O1 Pro with a 6.39-inch 1.5K wide-aspect flat screen and up to 16GB/1TB.
items.why: Two Weibo tipsters that GSMArena calls reliable say Osta will be printed on retail boxes. Positioning the phones as flagships contradicts an earlier leak of Kirin 8-series mid-rangers, and an earlier tipster warned the English name might differ. Huawei has not confirmed the brand. Update Nov 11: Richard Yu officially confirmed the OSTA name and a Nov 20 debut, and his Weibo posts show an 'OSTA O1 Pro' device label, matching the tipsters. The name and O1 Pro model are now confirmed; the quad-curved O1, flagship positioning and 16GB/1TB memory still come from leaks and retail-box photos, so the full claim moves to Likely. Update Nov 17: Huawei's Vmall pre-order page for the OSTA O1 Pro confirms memory options up to 16GB/1TB (16GB only in Starburst Purple) and three colors. The flagship-level specs and the quad-curved O1 still rest on leaks, so it stays Likely until the Nov 20 launch. Update Nov 20: Huawei launched OSTA and the O1 Pro as described: a 6.39-inch 1.5K 16:9.5 flat screen, up to 16GB/1TB, Kirin 9030S and a 200MP main camera, from 5,499 yuan. Huawei Central reports the O1 was shown too, but its quad-curved screen and specs were not detailed in the launch reports we found.
items.outcome: Mostly correct. The OSTA name, the wide-screen O1 Pro with a 6.39-inch 1.5K flat display and up to 16GB/1TB all matched the launch on Nov 20. The O1 Pro is priced from 5,499 yuan with a Kirin 9030S and 200MP camera, so 'flagship-level' fairly describes it. The quad-curved O1 was named and shown, but we could not confirm its specs or price.

items.title: Huawei Mate 80 Air launches in December
items.claim: Huawei will launch the Mate 80 Air thin phone next month, with the MatePad Mini 2 arriving separately, possibly also in December.
items.why: A single Weibo tipster via GSMArena. Another tipster said a few days ago that a Mate-series Air arrives within two months with 12GB of RAM and a circular camera island; the Kirin 9030 and curved screen are expected but unconfirmed. The Mate 70 Air launched about a year ago, so the timing is plausible, but Huawei has said nothing. Update Nov 19: Huawei officially announced a thin Mate phone for its Nov 24 event, but it is called the Mate 90 Air, and Vmall reservations are open with 12GB of RAM and 256GB/512GB storage.
items.outcome: Partly correct. Huawei's thin Mate phone is real and launches before the end of the year, but it is called the Mate 90 Air (Huawei skipped the 'Mate 80 Air' name) and it is unveiled on Nov 24, about a week before the December window. The 12GB of RAM and round camera island from the second tipster were right.

items.title: Redmi Turbo 6 Max packs an 11,000mAh battery
items.expected: Not announced (global version expected as Poco X9 Pro Max)
items.claim: The Redmi Turbo 6 Max will have an 11,000mAh (40.72Wh) battery, a 7-inch 2K 185Hz OLED and a Dimensity 9500s chip.
items.why: A tipster GSMArena calls reliable described a Dimensity performance phone with a 7-inch 2K screen and an 11,000mAh battery without naming it; the match to the Turbo 6 Max is GSMArena's inference from earlier leaks. That would be a big step from the Turbo 5 Max's 9,000mAh. Xiaomi has not announced the phone, and global Poco versions often ship with smaller batteries.

items.title: Apple makes Siri AI a proactive agent as early as 2027
items.claim: Apple will turn Siri AI into an agent that tracks goals and carries out multi-step tasks on its own, like OpenAI's Dots or Meta's Muse, possibly as soon as next year.
items.why: From Bloomberg's Mark Gurman in his Nov 8 Power On newsletter, relayed by MacRumors, 9to5Mac and Gizmodo. Gurman says he is told Apple ultimately wants Siri to work this way and that he believes it could happen as early as next year, and reports that CEO John Ternus pushed software chief Craig Federighi in a closed-door meeting to accelerate Apple's AI roadmap beyond Siri fixes. Gurman has a strong Apple record, but the timing is partly his own judgment, Apple has not committed to a release, and he also says Siri chief Mike Rockwell is still considering leaving. Rumor until there are concrete features or a version. Update Nov 19: Bloomberg spotted Apple job listings for a team building 'general-purpose computer-use agents' that browse the web, work across apps, run commands and write code, working with the Siri and Apple Foundation Models teams (MacRumors). That confirms Apple is building agents, but not that Siri ships as one in 2027, so the timing claim stays a Rumor.

items.title: One UI 9.5 lets Bixby run recurring tasks in the background
items.expected: With the Galaxy S27 series (early 2027, reported)
items.claim: Samsung's One UI 9.5 turns Bixby into a task agent that can run scheduled, recurring jobs in the background (for example a daily exchange-rate report), managed from a new Actions menu with an activity log.
items.why: Reported by SamMobile and relayed by GSMArena, which says the feature is in internal testing and expected to debut with the One UI 9.5-based Galaxy S27 series. SamMobile has good Samsung sources, but this is a single report, Samsung has not announced One UI 9.5 features, and features in internal testing can slip. Update Nov 18: the first One UI 9.5 beta changelog does not mention Bixby background tasks. That fits SamMobile's original report that the feature would debut with the Galaxy S27, so it stays a Rumor.

items.title: vivo has a 12,000mAh-plus phone battery in mass production
items.claim: vivo is already mass-producing a phone battery of 12,000mAh or more, with an even larger cell in development for a new large-screen device.
items.why: From a single Weibo post reported by IT Home and relayed by Gizchina. It names no phone or date and does not say whether 12,000mAh is the rated or typical capacity, which can differ noticeably. Chinese brands are clearly racing past 10,000mAh, so it is plausible, but vivo has not confirmed it. Update Nov 15: Digital Chat Station also says vivo is mass-producing the cell and gives its rated capacity as 11,970mAh (so roughly 12,000mAh typical), and that vivo is testing even larger batteries for big-screen devices (via GSMArena's week 46 recap). Still no phone or date; it stays a Rumor.

items.title: Galaxy S27 cameras: Ultra drops to a single 5x telephoto, S27 Pro gets a 10MP 3x zoom
items.claim: The Galaxy S27 and S27+ keep a 50MP main, 12MP ultrawide and 10MP 3x camera; the S27 Pro and Ultra share a 200MP ISOCELL HP6 main, a 50MP ultrawide and a 16MP selfie camera, but the Pro gets only a 10MP 3x telephoto and the Ultra a single 50MP 5x telephoto.
items.why: From SammyGuru, relayed by Android Authority and GSMArena, with specific sensor part numbers. It fits Ice Universe's August claim that the Ultra has only three rear cameras, and on Nov 10 he said the fourth camera shown on dummy units shared by Sonny Dickson 'does not exist'. The Pro's 10MP 3x camera contradicts earlier leaks of 50MP 5x or 3.5x options. One sourced leak, Samsung has said nothing, so it is a Rumor. Update Nov 16: Ice Universe posted what he calls the '100% confirmed' final camera layout for the S27 Pro and Ultra: a wide rectangular island with two large stacked lenses and one smaller lens, which fits three rear cameras. SamMobile's summary lists the Pro's 3x zoom as 12MP rather than 10MP, so the Pro telephoto spec is still unsettled. It stays a Rumor.

items.title: One UI 9.5 lets Galaxy phones record WhatsApp, Telegram and Google Meet calls
items.expected: One UI 9.5 (with the Galaxy S27 series, early 2027)
items.claim: Samsung's Phone app in One UI 9.5 adds a 'Record calls in other apps' setting with per-app toggles for VoIP calls in WhatsApp, Telegram and Google Meet, possibly limited by country.
items.why: SamMobile found and screenshotted the setting in One UI 9.5 software, which is hard evidence rather than a tip; Android Authority relays it. Samsung has not announced it, features in test builds can change, and availability may depend on local recording laws (some regions may announce the recording to the other caller). Update Nov 18: the first One UI 9.5 beta changelog for the Galaxy S26 does not mention recording calls in other apps. Samsung often holds features for the stable release with new phones, so it stays Likely, but it is now unconfirmed by the first official feature list.

items.title: OnePlus 17 gets a wide-screen display
items.claim: The OnePlus 17 will be one of five wide-screen flagship phones launching in 2027, with a wider (roughly 16:9 or 16:10) display aimed at gaming.
items.why: From Weibo tipster Smart Pikachu, relayed by GSMArena. It fits a run of similar reports about Oppo, vivo and Xiaomi wide-screen phones, but there are no specs and OnePlus has said nothing. The aspect-ratio figures come from the reports about the other brands.

items.title: Xiaomi 18 Pro reaches India in December, but the 18 Pro Max skips India
items.expected: December 2026 or early January 2027 (conflicting leaks; India model BIS-certified)
items.claim: After the Nov 17 global launch, only the Xiaomi 18 Pro comes to India, in December; the 18 Pro Max will not be sold there. The same tipster lists Xiaomi 18T specs (Dimensity 8600, 1.5K 165-185Hz OLED, IP69, 200MP main camera).
items.why: From a single tipster on X, relayed by GSMArena. It fits earlier reports that India may get only the 18 Pro, but Xiaomi has not announced Indian plans. The 18T specs have no timing; the 17T launched in May. Update Nov 13-14: the Indian Xiaomi 18 Pro (2609BPN61I) passed BIS certification (GSMArena), which supports an India launch. But tipster Abhishek Yadav (via The Tech Outlook) now says it launches in India in the first week of January 2027, with sales the following week, contradicting the December timing. With the leaks conflicting on the month this drops to Shaky; the 18 Pro Max skipping India is still uncontested but unconfirmed.

items.title: vivo X500 series costs INR 119,999-229,999 in India, launching late November
items.claim: The vivo X500 (12/256GB) will cost INR 119,999, the X500 Pro INR 149,999 and the X500 Pro Max INR 159,999 (INR 179,999 for 512GB; INR 229,999 for a 'master set'), with a launch toward the end of November.
items.why: A tipster on X calls these 'tentative' prices; GSMArena relays them. The phones are already out in China and globally, so an Indian launch is very likely, but vivo has not confirmed the date or prices. Update Nov 12: vivo India confirmed a Nov 26 launch, so the late-November timing is now official; the prices remain a tipster's tentative figures until launch.

items.title: Oppo A7 Ultra launches in December with a 12,000mAh battery
items.claim: Oppo will launch an A7 Ultra in December with a 12,000mAh battery and a large horizontal rear camera module.
items.why: The battery has hard evidence behind it: an Oppo phone numbered PNC110 appeared in China's MIIT database with a 12,000mAh cell, and updated MIIT images show a purple phone with a horizontal camera bar. The A7 Ultra name and December timing come only from tipster Digital Chat Station, who is usually reliable on Chinese phones, so linking PNC110 to the A7 Ultra is still an inference. Oppo has said nothing.

items.title: Honor is testing a 6.39-inch wide-screen phone with a 200MP camera and 8,000mAh battery
items.claim: A wide-screen phone with a 6.39-inch display, a Snapdragon chip, a 200MP main camera, a periscope telephoto and at least 8,000mAh of battery is in development, apparently from Honor.
items.why: Digital Chat Station posted the specs on Weibo but did not name the brand; GSMArena reads Honor from the emoji he used. The specs may be solid, but the brand is a guess and the device is an early engineering sample, so this is Shaky. It joins similar wide-screen reports about Oppo, vivo, Xiaomi, OnePlus and Huawei's OSTA.

items.title: Samsung is developing a phone whose screen slides up from 16:9 to 21:9
items.expected: No timeline (an earlier rumor said first half of 2028)
items.claim: Samsung is working on a phone with a vertically rolling display that extends from a 16:9 to a 21:9 aspect ratio, with battery capacity as the main challenge because of the sliding mechanism.
items.why: From leaker Ice Universe, who has a good Samsung record, relayed by GSMArena. It fits Samsung's 'Galaxy Z Roll' trademark, a side-rolling patent and a June rumor of a rollable in the first half of 2028, but there is no timing, model name or Samsung comment.

items.title: AMD's next Halo APU, 'Siren Halo', adds dedicated GDDR7 memory
items.expected: Not announced (successor to Gorgon Halo; no timing leaked)
items.claim: AMD's next big Ryzen AI Max APU is called Siren Halo, replacing the design previously known as Medusa Halo, and supports dedicated GDDR7 VRAM alongside LPDDR memory, possibly sharing RDNA 5 'AT2' graphics with the next Xbox's Magnus chip.
items.why: From hardware leaker Gotou_3rd on X, relayed by VideoCardz, which adds its own unnamed sources for the Xbox Magnus link; Gotou says that link is 'very likely' but unconfirmed. It fits Kepler_L2's Oct 30 claim that Medusa Halo was renamed. A GDDR7 pool would be a big change from today's LPDDR-only Halo chips. AMD has said nothing.

items.title: Apple is working on a bigger wide foldable, an 'iPhone Duo 2 Plus', to rival a Galaxy Z Fold 9 Plus
items.claim: Apple is developing a larger wide-format foldable, dubbed 'iPhone Duo 2 Plus', for 2027 to compete with a rumored bigger Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 9 Plus.
items.why: A single post on X from tipster TheGalox, relayed by GSMArena and Android Headlines; the name is likely a placeholder. Android Headlines calls it the first report of its kind for Apple and urges caution. A bigger or cheaper Fold 9 sibling has been rumored since late October, but the Apple half has no corroboration, and Apple only just launched its first foldable.

items.title: Samsung is testing a $4.99-a-month Galaxy AI Premium subscription
items.expected: Early-access test first; possibly around the Galaxy S27 launch (speculation)
items.claim: Samsung will offer a paid Galaxy AI Premium plan at $4.99 a month or $47.99 a year, with higher usage limits and paid-only features such as Gen Video, Bixby Action and Daily Briefing, while core features stay free with usage caps.
items.why: From SammyGuru (Nov 8), with screenshots of an opt-in early-access program in which test charges are refunded; relayed by SamMobile and Android Authority. Samsung told Tech Advisor that core Galaxy AI features will remain free but that some advanced capabilities or new services 'may be offered as paid options' in the future. That supports the idea of a paid tier but not the price, the feature list or the timing, which all rest on the one leak. Update Nov 15: screenshots from a leaked One UI 9.5 build, posted by the Telegram channel The Cipher Project and reported by Appdated, show a Galaxy AI Premium upsell with a 'Try free' button listing full access to a new Bixby Work agent, Gen Video and higher limits. It backs the existence of a paid tier with a free trial; price and timing still rest on the original leak.

items.title: SpaceX and Tesla could announce a merger as soon as December
items.claim: SpaceX and Tesla are progressing toward a merger that could be announced as soon as December 2026, though it may slip into early 2027.
items.why: Reported by Bloomberg, citing unnamed people familiar with the talks, and relayed by The Verge, Electrek and Quartz. The people say the boards and advisers are still negotiating terms, governance and the share exchange, and that keeping Tesla's China business apart from SpaceX's defense contracts is a complication. Bloomberg has a strong record, but this is one outlet's anonymous sourcing on a deal neither company has announced, and the reported deal values differ between outlets.

items.title: Galaxy S27 series comes in five colors: white, dark blue, light blue, pink and burgundy
items.claim: Samsung will offer the Galaxy S27 series in five colors matching leaked stock wallpapers: white/cream, dark blue, light blue, pink and burgundy.
items.why: Based on five color-matched stock wallpapers from what SammyGuru says are leaked firmware files, relayed by SamMobile, Android Authority and Android Police. Samsung usually ships wallpapers that match its phone colors, but wallpapers are not a color list, which models get which colors is unknown, and Samsung has said nothing.

items.title: Volkswagen's €20,000 entry-level EV will be called the ID. UP
items.expected: 2027 (VW has confirmed the car, not the name)
items.claim: The production version of Volkswagen's ID. EVERY1 concept, due in 2027 from about €20,000, will be sold as the ID. UP.
items.why: Volkswagen filed an 'ID. UP' trademark with the EU and German trademark offices on Oct 22, 2026 (reported by Electrek), and earlier reports said VW wanted to revive the Up! name. VW has confirmed the car, its 2027 timing and roughly €20,000 price, but not the name; carmakers often register names they never use.

items.title: Oppo's 'Fuyao' pocket gimbal camera debuts by the end of 2026
items.claim: Oppo will launch a pocket gimbal camera, codenamed Fuyao, before the end of 2026; its wide-screen foldable (likely Find N7) with a 2nm Snapdragon chip and a 16:9 'Reno X' bar phone are also near launch.
items.why: From Weibo tipster Digital Chat Station, relayed by GSMArena and Android Headlines. Earlier rumors gave the camera a 200MP 1/1.12-inch sensor and Hasselblad branding. Digital Chat Station has a decent record on Oppo, but this is one tipster with no official teaser, and the year-end timing leaves little room.

items.title: Huawei's next nova Flip becomes a small wide foldable with a Kirin 9-series chip
items.claim: Huawei will refresh the nova Flip line in 2027 with a small wide-aspect foldable that has a 6.3-inch screen and a Kirin 9-series chip.
items.why: From a single Weibo tipster, relayed by GSMArena. Digital Chat Station said in July that Huawei would release a new small wide foldable next year, which GSMArena had assumed was a Pura X successor. Plausible, but one source with no official word.

items.title: Honor's Magic10 series gets a 200MP LOFIC main camera and possibly a dual-layer OLED
items.expected: 2027 (Magic9 series launched in September 2026; no date leaked)
items.claim: Honor's next flagship line, the Magic10 series, will use a large 200MP main camera sensor with LOFIC (lateral overflow integration capacitor) tech for wider dynamic range, may bring back a variable aperture, and could use a dual-layer (tandem) OLED screen.
items.why: From Weibo tipster Smart Pikachu, relayed by GSMArena. The same tipster earlier suggested variable aperture is returning. On the screen, he only said Honor is evaluating dual-layer OLED for tablets and phones and tagged the post #HonorMagic10, while ruling out dual-layer OLED on all 2027 flagships. One tipster, no model named for the camera (GSMArena guesses the Magic10 Pro Max), and Honor has said nothing.

items.title: Samsung Health gets a Galaxy AI 'Scan meal' calorie estimator, possibly paid later
items.claim: Samsung Health will add Scan meal, a Galaxy AI feature that identifies food, ingredients and portion sizes from a photo and estimates calories; it is labeled beta and its terms say it could become a paid feature.
items.why: SamMobile found the feature inside the Samsung Health app, including Samsung's own beta label, accuracy warnings and a note that photos are processed on servers. That is hard evidence the feature exists, so it is Likely. The One UI 9.5 timing is SamMobile's expectation, and 'could become paid' is Samsung hedging, not a price. Update Nov 18: Samsung's official One UI 9.5 beta changelog for the Galaxy S26 lists 'Scan meals and log them instantly': one photo of a meal gives nutrition details, ingredients and a calorie estimate, available in the US only. The feature is real and part of One UI 9.5, so this resolves.
items.outcome: Correct on the feature: meal scanning with ingredient and calorie estimates is in Samsung's One UI 9.5 changelog. It arrived earlier than expected (in the Galaxy S26 beta on Nov 18 rather than first with the S27) and is US-only. Whether it becomes paid later is still unknown; the changelog says nothing about pricing.

items.title: Expert RAW gets a redesign, burst DNG mode and wider virtual aperture for the Galaxy S27
items.claim: Samsung's Expert RAW camera app will be redesigned for the Galaxy S27 and One UI 9.5, with two customizable buttons beside the shutter, a settings lock, a bigger RGB histogram, a separate tint control, a burst mode saving up to 30 DNG shots, virtual aperture from f/1.4 to f/22 (vs up to f/16 on the S26 Ultra), and signs of video recording.
items.why: SamMobile says it got access to an early version of the app and shows the new interface. That is hard evidence of work in progress, so it is Likely; Samsung may still change features, and video capture does not work in the build tested.

items.title: Meta's Muse Spark 1.4 is already in internal use
items.claim: Meta's next model, Muse Spark 1.4, is already running inside Meta's internal tools ahead of any public release.
items.why: A public pull request on Meta's RocksDB GitHub repository includes auto-generated test notes showing a real call to 'muse-spark-1.4-internal' (about 33,500 input tokens, 8,169 output tokens, 65 seconds), spotted by @LuminaBench and reported by TestingCatalog. That is hard evidence the model exists internally, so it is Likely. The internal name may change, and there is no word on release date, benchmarks or price; Meta has not commented.

items.title: The 'iPhone 20 Pro' uses iPhone Air-style glass that curves on all four sides
items.claim: Apple's 2027 anniversary Pro iPhones use the same glass material as the iPhone Air, shaped with more curvature so the front and back curve on all four edges around a thin polished metal frame.
items.why: From Weibo leaker Fixed Focus Digital, relayed by MacRumors, who earlier said Apple modified iPhone Air production equipment to make more rounded glass. The broad direction matches Bloomberg's Mark Gurman, who has reported glass curving into the sides on the anniversary Pro models. The material detail and the 'iPhone 20 Pro' name rest on one leaker, and Apple's naming is unknown, so it is a Rumor. Update Nov 17: Ice Universe posted videos of an 'approved' quad-curved cover glass sample and screen protectors with very thin borders and a Dynamic Island cutout (MacRumors, GSMArena). MacRumors notes such parts are often early manufacturing tests built from rumors rather than Apple's final specs, and they say nothing about the glass material, so this stays a Rumor.

items.title: Intel's Razor Lake desktop line gets a 12 P-core gaming chip with big cache and no regular E-cores
items.claim: Intel's 2028 Razor Lake-S lineup includes an unlocked '12+0+4' chip with 12 P-cores, four low-power E-cores and Intel's big Last Level Cache (bLLC), built on Intel 18A-P, replacing a planned 8+0+4 part; a 6+12+4 bLLC chip moves from Nova Lake to Razor Lake.
items.why: From Intel leaker Jaykihn on X, reported by TechPowerUp. He has a decent record on Intel roadmaps, and Intel has listed Razor Lake model IDs in its ISA reference, but none of these configurations are official and plans two years out often change. One source, so it is a Rumor.

items.title: One UI 9.5 adds a 'Daily Brief' that summarizes your emails and app notifications
items.expected: One UI 9.5 (with or after the Galaxy S27)
items.claim: Samsung's Now Brief gains a Daily Brief that pulls notifications from apps such as WhatsApp, Telegram, LINE, KakaoTalk and SMS/RCS plus your email, and sorts them into cards for finance and payments, bookings and appointments, and work email at a set time of day.
items.why: From an Android Authority APK teardown of Samsung's Personal Agent Core package, with developer strings naming the feature and its card categories. Code evidence shows Samsung is building it, but Android Authority stresses the code is work in progress and may not ship, and it suggests these agent features may sit in a paid Galaxy AI tier. Samsung has said nothing, so it is a Rumor. Update Nov 18: SamMobile published screenshots of the feature working (as 'Daily Briefing'), with reminder cards built from payment notices, maintenance fees, appointments and email deadlines, grouped into categories such as Finance, Work and Productivity, and Mobility and Traffic (relayed by Android Authority). SamMobile also showed a related Recall card that pulls reservations and tickets from Gmail. Screenshots of a working build from a second outlet move this to Likely. It is not in the first One UI 9.5 beta changelog, it may launch with the Galaxy S27 instead, and it appears on a leaked list of paid Galaxy AI Premium features.

items.title: Lenovo's Googlebook Duet 13 detachable launches in January
items.claim: Lenovo's first detachable Googlebook, the Googlebook Duet 13, with a 13-inch screen, a detachable keyboard, a stylus and a kickstand cover, launches in January 2027.
items.why: From Evan Blass, who shared new images and said it is 'launching in January' (via 9to5Google and Android Authority). Google has already teased detachable Googlebooks as coming soon, and Blass's leaked images and track record are strong, so the product looks real and the timing is Likely. Lenovo and Google have not announced a date, name or price.

items.title: Variable aperture returns on the Galaxy S28 Pro and S28 Ultra, not the S27
items.claim: Samsung brings back a variable-aperture main camera on the Galaxy S28 Pro and S28 Ultra, which implies the Galaxy S27 Pro and Ultra keep fixed apertures.
items.why: From a single tipster on X, relayed by SamMobile and GSMArena. Apple added variable aperture to the iPhone 18 Pro this year and Honor is reportedly bringing it back, so the idea is plausible, but an earlier Ice Universe claim that the S26 Ultra would get it did not pan out, and the S28 is more than a year away. Samsung has said nothing.

items.title: Oppo's next Pro Max hides its bezels under four-sided curved glass (about 0.3mm)
items.expected: Next Find X flagship series (likely Find X11 Pro Max; no date)
items.claim: Oppo's next top flagship, likely the Find X11 Pro Max, pairs a flat panel with cover glass curved on all four sides for a visual bezel of about 0.3mm; the tech is pricey, so only top models get it and OnePlus stays flat.
items.why: From Digital Chat Station on Weibo (via GSMArena), who called it a 'super early preview' and answered 'PM' when asked which phone gets it. DCS has a good record on Oppo, and it fits last week's report that the Find X11 Pro Max inherits parts from the reportedly suspended Find X10 Ultra. It is one tipster, very early, and Oppo has not commented.

items.title: Huawei Watch Air is a 6.9mm titanium smartwatch with up to 5 days of battery
items.claim: Huawei's upcoming Watch Air has a 6.9mm titanium unibody, an irregular high-silicon stacked battery (over 10% silicon) for up to five days of use, Watch GT 7 Pro-level activity tracking and Watch 6 sensors including ECG.
items.why: From Weibo tipster Fixed Focus Digital, relayed by GSMArena with leaked images. The name and thin design have been rumored before, but the specs come from one leaker and Huawei has not announced the watch or a date. Update Nov 19: Huawei's official teaser confirms the Watch Air name, the 6.9mm thickness and a titanium unibody, with launch on Nov 24. The battery is still unconfirmed, and Digital Chat Station now says about a week rather than five days, so the claim moves to Likely until launch.

items.title: Samsung held Quick Share's Tap to Share back for One UI 9.5
items.expected: One UI 9.5 (with the Galaxy S27 series, early 2027)
items.claim: Quick Share's NFC Tap to Share, which Google promised for the Galaxy Z8 foldables 'soon' after the Pixel 11 launch, arrives on Galaxy phones with One UI 9.5 rather than earlier.
items.why: The Cipher Project on Telegram (via Android Authority) found a complete 'Tap to share' settings page in the latest Quick Share and Connectivity apps that only appears when a device is spoofed as One UI 9.5. Working code in shipping apps is hard evidence and the feature is officially promised, so it is Likely; Samsung has not confirmed the timing, and it could still arrive earlier through an app update. Update Nov 18: Tap to Share is not in the changelog for the first One UI 9.5 beta on the Galaxy S26, which does not rule it out for later betas or the stable release with the Galaxy S27. It stays Likely.

items.title: The 'iPhone 20 Pro' gets a new main camera sensor with a 17nm image processor
items.claim: Apple's 2027 anniversary Pro iPhones use a new main camera sensor paired with a new image signal processor built on a 17nm process.
items.why: From Ice Universe on Weibo, relayed by GSMArena. A new sensor is expected for a flagship redesign, but the 17nm ISP detail is from one leaker with no stated benefits, and Apple's naming and specs are unknown.

items.title: One Galaxy S27 model gets an 'extremely bezel-less' display
items.expected: Early 2027 (Galaxy S27 launch), if at all
items.claim: A Samsung supplier is preparing an 'extremely bezel-less' display, and Samsung may pull it forward into one of the Galaxy S27 models, most likely the Ultra or Pro.
items.why: From Korean leaker Lanzuk on Naver, citing a Samsung supplier, relayed by 9to5Google and GSMArena. The original post is vague, machine translation does not clarify what 'extremely bezel-less' means, the leaker himself sounds unsure, and 9to5Google calls it about a 50/50 shot. Which model would get it is pure speculation. It also sits awkwardly with Ice Universe's earlier, much more modest 1.28mm S27 Ultra bezel figure.

items.title: The iQOO Z12 Lite is a renamed Z11 Lite with a Dimensity 6300
items.claim: iQOO's next budget phone, the Z12 Lite (model I2510), uses the MediaTek Dimensity 6300 with 4GB or 6GB of RAM, a 720x1600 screen with a waterdrop notch and Android 16, the same specs as the Z11 Lite.
items.why: The specs come from a Google Play Console listing (via GSMArena), which is hard evidence and usually means a launch is close; the same entry lists the Z11 Lite (I2515) as a variant, hence the rebrand reading. A separate 5G 'Z12 Lite' (I2603) reportedly passed Bluetooth SIG, so there may be different versions by market, and iQOO has not announced the phone or a date.

items.title: Google's Pixel Tag goes on sale in the EU 'pretty soon'
items.claim: Google will start selling the Pixel Tag Find Hub tracker in European Union countries soon; it launched with the Pixel 11 in eight countries including the UK but none in the EU.
items.why: From leaker Roland Quandt on Bluesky (via 9to5Google), who has a strong record on European retail plans. It is one short post with no date, markets or price, and Google has said nothing about EU availability.

items.title: Apple is developing four 20th-anniversary iPhones in two designs, curved and flat
items.claim: Apple is working on four anniversary iPhone models: two with glass curving along all four edges and roughly 1mm bezels, and two with flat cover glass.
items.why: From Ice Universe on Weibo, relayed by MacRumors and 9to5Mac. It fits Gurman's August report that Apple toned down a more radical anniversary design but still uses curved front and rear glass. What the flat models are is unclear: MacRumors suggests they could be fallback versions of the Pro and Pro Max or standard models launching later, so this does not mean Apple will sell four new designs. One leaker, no official word.

items.title: Apple may delay or cancel its OLED iMac
items.expected: Previously 2029-2030; a new LCD iMac reportedly around 2029
items.claim: Apple is talking to Samsung Display about delaying, or possibly shelving, the OLED iMac because of high panel costs and weak OLED demand, and has asked LCD makers including BOE for panels for an iMac around 2029.
items.why: From Korea's The Elec citing industry sources, relayed by MacRumors and 9to5Mac. One source said talks focus on a delay rather than cancellation. It fits weak OLED iPad Pro sales and rising memory costs, but in October Mark Gurman said Apple was still testing OLED for the iMac and MacBook Air. Single-outlet supply-chain report; Apple never announced an OLED iMac.

items.title: Foxconn will assemble OpenAI's first smartphone, due late 2027 or 2028
items.claim: Foxconn subsidiary FIH Mobile has won the order to assemble OpenAI's first smartphone, with Apple suppliers Luxshare, Lingyi iTech and AAC supplying parts, for a debut in late 2027 or 2028.
items.why: From Chinese outlets Securities Times and Cailian Press citing supply-chain sources, relayed by Android Authority. Ming-Chi Kuo earlier reported an OpenAI phone with a custom MediaTek chip and named Luxshare as its manufacturing partner. Neither OpenAI nor Foxconn has confirmed anything, and this is separate from OpenAI's first Jony Ive device (see the launch calendar).

items.title: Samsung readies 14- and 16-inch Android laptops codenamed 'Origin' with Snapdragon X Elite
items.expected: Around or after the Galaxy S27 launch (early 2027, speculation)
items.claim: Samsung is building two Wi-Fi-only Android laptops, codenamed origin14 and origin16 (model numbers XE940XSA and XE960XSA), with a 12-core Snapdragon X Elite; the 16-inch model may have a touchscreen.
items.why: Android Authority found the codenames, model numbers and chip profile in Samsung's own One UI 9.5 beta code, and an XE940XSA running Android 17 on a Snapdragon X Elite appeared on Geekbench in October. That is hard evidence of real devices. The branding (Googlebook or not), price and launch timing are unknown; the timing is Android Authority's guess. Update Nov 20: SamMobile found One UI 9.5 code showing Samsung will push its own Googlebook OS firmware updates to the Origin laptops, with a Samsung setup wizard, RAM Plus and McAfee scans but no Maintenance Mode. More evidence the laptops are real; still no name, price or date, so it stays Likely.

items.title: Samsung's Galaxy Studio over-ear headphones have an 870mAh battery, ANC and wired audio
items.claim: Samsung's upcoming Galaxy Studio headphones have an 870mAh battery, USB-C charging and wired audio (plus 3.5mm support), ANC, wear detection, touch controls, 360 Audio with head tracking, Auracast and Samsung Find.
items.why: SammyGuru found the headphones and their feature list in Samsung's One UI 9.5 firmware, reported by SamMobile, Android Authority and The Verge. Firmware references are strong evidence that the product exists, but whether it has a dedicated 3.5mm port is unclear, and price and launch date are unknown.

items.title: One UI 9.5 adds Open Gate full-sensor video and a front-and-rear 'dual cam panorama'
items.expected: A later One UI 9.5 update or the Galaxy S27 (early 2027)
items.claim: Samsung's Camera app will offer Open Gate video that records the full sensor area (24 to 60 fps) and a Dual cam panorama that uses the front and rear cameras together for a 360-degree shot.
items.why: Android Authority found strings for both features in the One UI 9.5 beta Camera app, relayed by GSMArena and SamMobile. Code is solid evidence Samsung is working on them, but code features do not always ship, and which phones get them is unknown.

items.title: Honor Magic V7 is a wide foldable, with no regular-shaped Magic V model next year
items.claim: Honor's next book-style foldable, the Magic V7, uses a wide form factor, and Honor won't release a conventional tall foldable alongside it.
items.why: From a tipster on X, reported by GSMArena. An earlier leak described an Honor wide foldable with a Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6, a 7.6-inch inner screen, a 5.5-inch cover screen and over 7,000mAh from CNY 9,999, but it did not name the model. Honor has not announced anything.

items.title: Motorola Razr Flex 2027 uses an unreleased Snapdragon 8 Gen 5 Pro
items.claim: The Razr Flex 2027 (XT2761, codename Parker), a compact wide foldable, runs Android 17 on Qualcomm's unannounced SM8845 Pro chip, with an under-display fingerprint reader and Bluetooth 6.0.
items.why: Android Authority cites a security certification document for the XT2761, a model number already tied to the Razr Flex 27 in UAE filings, and the phone appeared on Motorola's own website earlier this month. A certification listing is good evidence for the chip; the 'Snapdragon 8 Gen 5 Pro' name is the expected branding, not confirmed. A rear photo from Reddit is unverified, and the in-display fingerprint contradicts earlier leaks. Update Nov 20: GSMArena also reports the TrustCB listing (SM8845 Pro, Bluetooth 6.0, face unlock, under-display fingerprint) and notes a tipster says the same chip may be branded Snapdragon 8 Gen 6 in the OnePlus Turbo 7 Pro, so the final name is still open. It expects a mid-December launch. Stays Likely.

items.title: iPhone 20 Pro brings back a titanium frame
items.claim: Apple has started early engineering work on a titanium frame for the curved 2027 iPhone 20 Pro, similar to the iPhone Air's but more rounded, ending two generations of aluminum Pro frames.
items.why: From Weibo tipster Fixed Focus Digital, relayed by GSMArena; the same tipster is behind our iPhone 20 Pro curved-glass rumor. 'Early-stage engineering work' does not mean Apple has decided, and Apple has said nothing. One leaker, so it is a Rumor.

items.title: Tesla builds a driverless Model Y with no steering wheel or pedals for 6-7 people
items.claim: Tesla plans an autonomous version of the Model Y with no steering wheel or pedals, aimed at carrying groups of six or seven people.
items.why: Elon Musk said this on stage at the New York Times DealBook Summit on Nov 18 (Electrek, InsideEVs). It comes from Tesla's CEO, but there is no timeline, price, factory or regulatory path. A second car without controls would also face the same federal safety-standard fight as the Cybercab, and Musk's product timelines have a poor track record. We rate it a Rumor until Tesla puts a product and date behind it.

items.title: AMD's Zen 6 desktop CPUs move to TSMC N2X and slip to the second half of 2027
items.expected: Second half of 2027 (leaker; possibly after Computex in June)
items.claim: AMD's Olympic Ridge desktop Ryzen chips switched to TSMC's performance-focused N2X process, pushing their launch from the first half to the second half of 2027.
items.why: From Chiphell leaker Zhang Zhonghao, relayed by VideoCardz and PC Gamer. N2X enters production in 2027, which would fit a later launch and earlier rumors of very high clock speeds, and the post's mention of Computex is others' reading, not a stated date. It is one leaker, it conflicts with earlier reports of a CES reveal and spring retail, and AMD's Jack Huynh is teasing CES news. Rumor.

items.title: Meta's Muse Charm costs $300 and includes free Verizon 5G
items.claim: Meta will sell the Muse Charm, its keychain-sized gadget for talking to the Muse AI agent, for $300 with up to 12 months of free Verizon 5G data, and it uses a fingerprint reader to verify the user.
items.why: Reported by The Information and relayed by Engadget and The Verge; Meta did not comment. The device itself is official (shown at Connect in September for the holidays), but the price and Verizon deal come from one outlet's sources. The Information is usually well sourced, so this is a solid Rumor until Meta prices it.

items.title: Samsung raises US prices on eight Galaxy A phones by Jan 1, with the A57 at $599
items.claim: Samsung will raise prices on eight Galaxy A models in the US and other countries by January 1 because of memory costs, including the Galaxy A57 to $599, the A37 to $499, the A17 5G to $319 and the A07 5G to $229.
items.why: From Seoul Economic Daily citing industry sources, via SammyFans and Android Police. Memory prices really are rising and Samsung already raised some prices this year, which makes it plausible. But it is one report, some of the 'old' prices it lists don't match current US prices, and Samsung has said nothing. Rumor.

items.title: Xiaomi 19 series mixes flat and curved screens
items.expected: Next Xiaomi flagship generation (late 2027, no date; name not final)
items.claim: Development of Xiaomi's next flagship series has started, and the lineup will include both flat and curved cover glass.
items.why: From tipster Smart Pikachu on Weibo (via GSMArena). He did not say which models get which screen or how many models there will be, and says only a codename exists so far, so even the 'Xiaomi 19' name is uncertain. The split mirrors rumors for Apple's 2027 iPhones. Early, thin and unverifiable. Rumor.
